Add high-speed IO (PCIe, USB, Ethernet), the clock and reset generator with PLLs, the power-management controller, an interrupt controller, a boot ROM and security block, and the debug and JTAG port.

questions.q: Draw the microarchitecture of a CPU.
questions.st: Arm Graduate Hardware Engineer Cambridge Cambridgeshire interview
questions.a: Front end: PC, branch predictor and BTB, instruction cache and TLB, fetch queue and decoders. For an out-of-order core: rename map and physical register file, dispatch into reservation stations or issue queues, multiple execution units (ALUs, branch, multiply, FPU and SIMD, load-store units with a load-store queue and data cache), a reorder buffer for in-order retirement, and the L2 cache interface. For an in-order core, draw the five-stage pipeline with forwarding.

questions.q: Explain branch prediction.
questions.st: Arm Cpu Design Verification Madison Wisconsin interview
questions.a: Branch prediction guesses the outcome and target of a branch before it executes, so the pipeline keeps fetching. Static prediction (backward taken, forward not taken) is simplest. Dynamic predictors use 2-bit saturating counters per branch, correlate with global or local history (gshare, two-level, tournament, TAGE), use a branch target buffer for targets and a return address stack for returns. On a mispredict the wrong-path instructions are flushed, costing roughly the pipeline depth in cycles.

questions.q: Explain dynamic, static and short-circuit power: where and how each happens, and how to reduce it at the logic and architecture level.
questions.st: Arm Verification Engineer Manipal Karnataka interview
questions.a: Dynamic (switching) power is C V^2 f alpha, from charging and discharging load capacitance: reduce it by clock gating, lower activity (operand isolation, encoding), lower voltage and frequency (DVFS), and smaller capacitance. Short-circuit power flows briefly while both PMOS and NMOS are on during slow input transitions: reduce it with sharp input slews and balanced sizing. Static (leakage) power flows even when idle, through subthreshold, gate and junction leakage: reduce it with high-Vt cells, power gating, body biasing and lower voltage.

questions.q: Explain in-order versus out-of-order processors and register renaming.
questions.st: Arm Cpu Design Verification Madison Wisconsin interview
questions.a: An in-order processor issues instructions in program order, so one stalled instruction (for example waiting on a cache miss) blocks everything behind it. An out-of-order processor lets later independent instructions execute first, keeping execution units busy, and commits results in order through a reorder buffer. Register renaming makes this possible by mapping architectural registers to more physical registers, removing the false WAR and WAW dependencies caused by register reuse.

questions.q: Find K and Vth for an enhancement MOSFET with ID(on) = 325 mA at 12 V and 87.62 mA at 7 V.
questions.st: ARM interview questions (MOSFET, CMOS) 2021
questions.a: In saturation ID = K (VGS - Vt)^2. The ratio gives 325 / 87.62 = 3.709, so (12 - Vt) / (7 - Vt) = sqrt(3.709) = 1.926. Then 12 - Vt = 13.48 - 1.926 Vt, so Vt = 1.48 / 0.926 = about 1.6 V. Then K = 325 mA / (12 - 1.6)^2 = 325 / 108.2 = about 3.0 mA/V^2. (If the model uses ID = (K/2)(VGS - Vt)^2, K is twice that, about 6 mA/V^2.)

questions.q: Given a black box with some inputs, outputs and a timing diagram, how would you verify it?
questions.st: Arm Graduate Cpu Verification Antibes Provence Alpes Cote Dazur interview

Build a reference model of the expected behaviour, drive directed tests reproducing the diagram, then random stimulus within the protocol rules, and compare outputs with the model in a scoreboard. Add assertions for the timing relationships (for example ack within N cycles of req) and coverage for every input combination and protocol phase.

questions.q: In a given bus architecture, which are the masters and slaves, and how many addresses fit in a given range?
questions.st: Arm Graduate Hardware Engineer Budapest interview
questions.a: Masters start transactions (CPU, DMA, GPU); slaves respond (memory, peripherals, register blocks); bridges and the interconnect are slaves on one side and masters on the other. The number of addresses in a range is end - start + 1: for example 0x4000_0000 to 0x4000_FFFF is 0x10000 = 65,536 byte addresses (64 KB). Check the decoder: ranges must not overlap, and unmapped addresses should return an error response.

questions.st: Arm Hardwaredesign And Verification United Kingdom interview

Get bit i with (n >> i) & 1 and bit j with (n >> j) & 1 (or index the binary string bin(n)[2:] from the right), compare them and print True or False. In Python: n, i, j = map(int, s.split(',')); print(((n >> i) & 1) == ((n >> j) & 1)). Handle bad input and bit indexes beyond the number's width.

questions.q: What are semaphores and why are they used?
questions.st: Arm Cpu Verification New York New York interview
questions.a: A semaphore is a synchronisation object holding a count of available keys. get or wait decrements it and blocks if no key is available; put or signal increments it and wakes a waiter. A binary semaphore (one key) gives mutual exclusion over a shared resource; a counting semaphore limits access to N resources. In SystemVerilog testbenches, semaphores make sure, for example, that only one thread drives a shared bus at a time.

questions.q: What are the key features of the Arm architecture?
questions.st: Arm Hardware Engineer Cambridge Cambridgeshire interview
questions.a: A RISC load-store architecture with fixed-length instructions; a large register file (31 general registers in AArch64); simple addressing modes; conditional execution (AArch32) and condition flags; the compact Thumb instruction set; NEON and SVE SIMD; TrustZone security; exception levels EL0 to EL3 for user, OS, hypervisor and secure monitor; a weakly ordered memory model with barriers; and the AMBA bus ecosystem. Its strength is performance per watt and a licensing model used across mobile, embedded and servers.

questions.q: What is an MMU and what does it do?
questions.st: ARM interview experience for verification engineer intern (on-campus, virtual)
questions.a: The memory management unit translates the virtual addresses used by software into physical addresses using page tables, caching recent translations in a TLB. It also enforces access permissions per page (read, write, execute, user or privileged), sets memory attributes such as cacheability, and raises page faults or exceptions on illegal or unmapped accesses, which enables virtual memory and process isolation.

questions.q: What is an abstract class? What is the difference between a deep copy and a shallow copy?
questions.st: Arm Hardware Engineer Intern Cambridge Cambridgeshire interview
questions.a: An abstract class cannot be instantiated; it defines a common interface (often with pure virtual methods) that derived classes must implement. In SystemVerilog you write virtual class; in C++ a class with a pure virtual function. A shallow copy copies the object's members, but handles inside it still point to the same sub-objects, so both copies share them; a deep copy also creates new copies of the contained objects, so the copies are fully independent. In SystemVerilog, new with an existing handle does a shallow copy; deep copy needs a custom copy() method.

questions.q: What is inside a processor?
questions.st: Arm Cpu Design Verification Biot Provence Alpes Cote Dazur interview
questions.a: A control unit, a datapath (register file, ALU, shifter, multiplier and FPU), the program counter and fetch logic, decode logic, pipeline registers, load-store units, caches and TLBs, a bus interface, and interrupt and exception handling. High-end cores add branch predictors, register renaming, schedulers, a reorder buffer and SIMD units.

questions.q: What is paging?
questions.st: ARM interview experience for verification engineer intern (on-campus, virtual)
questions.a: Paging divides virtual memory into fixed-size pages (often 4 KB) and physical memory into frames of the same size. A page table maps each virtual page to a frame, with valid, permission and dirty bits; multi-level tables keep the table small. A TLB caches recent mappings. If a page is not in memory, a page fault lets the OS load it from disk. Paging avoids external fragmentation and makes allocation simple.

questions.q: What is the MMU?
questions.st: Arm Verification Engineer Canada interview
questions.a: The memory management unit is the hardware between the CPU and memory that translates virtual addresses to physical ones using page tables and a TLB, checks access permissions, and reports faults to the operating system. It is what makes virtual memory, protection between processes and demand paging possible.

questions.q: What is the transit time of a MOSFET with a 180 nm channel, Vds = 3 V and mobility 750?
questions.st: ARM interview questions (MOSFET, CMOS) 2021
questions.a: Transit time is roughly the channel length divided by the carrier velocity: t = L / (mu E) = L^2 / (mu VDS). With L = 180 nm = 1.8e-5 cm, mu = 750 cm^2/V.s and VDS = 3 V: t = (1.8e-5)^2 / (750 x 3) = 3.24e-10 / 2250 = about 1.4e-13 s, so around 0.14 ps. In a real short-channel device the carriers hit velocity saturation (about 1e7 cm/s), giving L / vsat = about 1.8 ps.

Make sure the address is aligned to the access size.

questions.q: Explain how physical design works.
questions.st: Arm Hardware Engineer Cambridge Massachusetts interview
questions.a: Physical design turns the synthesized netlist into a layout. Floorplanning sets the die size, places macros and IO, and builds the power grid. Placement puts standard cells to minimise wire length and congestion while meeting timing. Clock tree synthesis builds a balanced clock network with controlled skew. Routing connects every net with metal layers. Then sign-off: STA with extracted parasitics, IR drop and EM, signal integrity, DRC, LVS and antenna checks, with ECOs to fix issues, ending in GDSII for tape-out.

questions.q: How does the Karatsuba algorithm reduce the work of multiplying very large numbers?
questions.st: Arm Hardware Engineer Italy interview
questions.a: Schoolbook multiplication of two n-digit numbers needs n^2 digit multiplications. Karatsuba splits each number into high and low halves, x = a B + b and y = c B + d, and computes ac, bd and (a + b)(c + d) with three multiplications instead of four, since ad + bc = (a + b)(c + d) - ac - bd. Applied recursively this gives about n^1.585 operations, which is much faster for large numbers, and is used in big-integer and cryptography hardware.

questions.q: How would you compress a program trace coming straight from a CPU?
questions.st: Arm Systems Architect Cambridge Cambridgeshire interview
questions.a: Exploit how predictable a trace is. Program counters mostly increase sequentially, so emit only branch outcomes (taken or not taken bits) and targets of indirect branches, as Arm CoreSight and Intel PT do; a decoder rebuilds the full flow from the program binary. Encode addresses as deltas from the previous address with variable-length encoding, and timestamps as deltas, then apply run-length or dictionary compression on repeated patterns. This compresses the stream by one to two orders of magnitude.

questions.q: How does the SPI protocol work?
questions.st: Arm Hardware Engineer Intern Sheffield England interview
questions.a: SPI is a synchronous, full-duplex serial bus with one master and one or more slaves. It uses SCLK (the clock from the master), MOSI (master out), MISO (master in) and an active-low chip select per slave. The master pulls a slave's chip select low and toggles SCLK; on each clock edge one bit shifts out on MOSI and one bit in on MISO, usually MSB first. The clock polarity and phase (CPOL and CPHA, modes 0 to 3) set which edge samples. There is no addressing or acknowledgement in the protocol.

questions.q: Explain the UVM factory and config_db.
questions.st: Arm Verification Engineer Sheffield England interview
questions.a: The factory creates components and objects through type_id::create() instead of new, so a test can replace a type with a derived one without changing the environment: set_type_override_by_type() replaces it everywhere, set_inst_override_by_type() only at a given hierarchy path. config_db is a hierarchical database for passing configuration: set(context, path, name, value) stores a value (for example a virtual interface or a config object) and get() retrieves it in the build_phase of the component that matches the path.

Rewrite it with always_ff for flops (non-blocking), always_comb for logic with defaults, typed logic signals and parameters, and check it with a testbench.

It ends with endclass. In run_phase, the test raises an objection, starts the sequence, and drops the objection; run_test() in the top module starts it.

questions.q: What is UVM used for, and what is config_db?
questions.st: Arm Verification Engineer Austin Texas interview
questions.a: UVM is a standard SystemVerilog class library and methodology for building reusable, constrained-random, coverage-driven testbenches, with components (agents, drivers, monitors, scoreboards), phasing, the factory, TLM communication and sequences. config_db is its hierarchical configuration database: higher levels set values such as virtual interfaces, configuration objects and knobs for a path, and lower components get them in their build_phase, so components stay reusable.

questions.q: What is an abstraction technique in formal verification?
questions.st: Arm Verification Engineer Canada interview
questions.a: Abstraction simplifies the design so the formal tool can prove properties that would otherwise blow up in state space. Examples: cutting signals into free inputs (black-boxing a block), replacing a large counter or memory with a smaller abstract model, data-type reduction (prove for a few data bits instead of 64), and assume-guarantee decomposition. The abstraction must over-approximate behaviour, so a proof on it still holds for the real design; spurious counter-examples are refined away.

questions.q: What is formal verification, and how does it differ from random verification?
questions.st: Arm Verification Engineer Canada interview
questions.a: Formal verification proves properties mathematically for every possible input sequence from reset, using model checking or equivalence engines; it either gives a proof or a counter-example trace. Random (constrained-random simulation) verification samples the input space with stimulus and checks the responses, so it can only find bugs in the scenarios it happens to hit, measured by coverage. Formal is exhaustive but struggles with large designs and long sequences; simulation scales but is never complete.

questions.q: What is the cone of influence of a check in formal verification?
questions.st: Arm Verification Engineer Canada interview
questions.a: The cone of influence of a property is the set of signals and state elements that can affect it, found by tracing backwards from the signals in the property through the logic to the inputs. Formal tools only analyse this cone and ignore everything else, which reduces the state space. Keeping properties local and cutting irrelevant logic keeps the cone small and the proof tractable.

questions.q: Explain the regions of operation of a CMOS inverter and draw its transfer curve.
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Avago)
questions.a: Plot Vout against Vin. Region A (Vin < Vtn): NMOS off, PMOS linear, Vout = VDD. Region B: NMOS saturated, PMOS linear, output starts to fall. Region C (around the switching threshold VM): both saturated, very high gain, steep drop. Region D: NMOS linear, PMOS saturated. Region E (Vin > VDD - |Vtp|): PMOS off, NMOS linear, Vout = 0. VM is set by the PMOS-to-NMOS strength ratio; the slope of -1 points define VIL and VIH and the noise margins.

questions.q: Implement a ring oscillator. How do you slow it down?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Avago)
questions.a: Connect an odd number of inverters in a loop: no stable state exists, so it oscillates with period T = 2 N td, where N is the number of stages and td the delay per inverter. To slow it down, add more stages (keeping the count odd), add load capacitance or use current-starved inverters (limit each stage's current with extra transistors controlled by a bias voltage, which makes it a VCO), or divide the output frequency with a counter.

questions.q: C1 = 10 pF and C2 = 1 pF are in series with a switch between them; one end is at 5 V, the other at 0 V. What is the voltage across C2 when the switch closes?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Avago)
questions.a: Assuming both capacitors start uncharged, in series they get the same charge, so the voltages split in inverse proportion to capacitance: V across C2 = 5 V x C1 / (C1 + C2) = 5 x 10 / 11 = about 4.55 V, and about 0.45 V across C1. The smaller capacitor takes most of the voltage. If they were pre-charged, charge conservation on the node between them would decide the answer instead.

questions.q: Compare FIR and IIR filters.
questions.st: Broadcom Wireless Systems Verification Intern San Diego Ca interview
questions.a: An FIR (finite impulse response) filter uses only current and past inputs: y[n] = sum of b_k x[n-k]. It is always stable, can have exactly linear phase, and is easy to pipeline, but needs many taps for sharp responses. An IIR (infinite impulse response) filter also feeds back past outputs, so it reaches a sharp response with far fewer coefficients and less hardware, but it can be unstable, has non-linear phase, and is sensitive to coefficient quantisation and overflow.

questions.q: How do a sampling scope and a real-time scope work?
questions.st: Broadcom Validation Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: A real-time scope digitises the signal continuously at a sample rate several times its bandwidth, so it captures single-shot events. A sampling (equivalent-time) scope takes one sample per trigger at a slightly shifted delay each time and rebuilds a repetitive waveform, reaching very high bandwidths (tens of GHz) with slow ADCs, but it only works for repetitive signals such as eye diagrams.

questions.q: How do you debug failing serial and parallel pattern simulations?
questions.st: Broadcom Staff Dft Engineer United States interview
questions.a: Start by deciding whether the problem is in shift or capture. Run a chain integrity (flush) test first: if it fails in serial simulation, check scan connectivity, clocks and reset during shift, lockup latches and test-mode setup. Parallel simulation forces the chain values directly, so a pattern that passes in parallel but fails in serial points to shift problems; failures in both point to capture problems: timing (need SDF annotation), uninitialised X sources, clocking, constraints mismatch with ATPG, or bus contention. Compare the failing flop and cycle with the ATPG expected values.

questions.st: Broadcom Staff Dft Engineer United States interview

Local comparators sit next to each memory: they allow parallel testing and faster diagnosis, at a higher area cost. The choice trades area against test time and power.

They are fixed with test points, test-mode muxes and constraints.

questions.q: What are static class members?
questions.st: Broadcom Verification Engineer San Jose Ca interview
questions.a: A static class member (a static property or method) belongs to the class rather than to each object: there is a single copy shared by all instances. A static property can count objects created or hold a shared configuration; static methods can only access static members and can be called with class_name::method() without creating an object. The UVM singleton patterns use this.

questions.q: What is IR drop?
questions.st: Broadcom Hardware Engineer San Diego Ca interview
questions.a: IR drop is the voltage lost along the power and ground network because of its resistance (V = I R), so cells see less than the nominal supply. Static IR drop uses average currents; dynamic IR drop uses simultaneous switching current peaks. Lower supply slows cells and can cause timing failures or functional errors. Fix it with a denser or wider power grid, more vias and pins, decap cells, and spreading high-activity logic.

questions.q: What is a PLL?
questions.st: Broadcom Validation Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: A phase-locked loop generates a stable, high-frequency clock locked to a reference. A phase-frequency detector compares the reference with the divided output, a charge pump and loop filter turn the error into a control voltage, and a voltage-controlled oscillator produces the output; a divider by N in the feedback makes fout = N x fref. PLLs are used for clock multiplication, de-skewing, frequency synthesis and clock recovery.

questions.q: What is a pull-up resistor used for?
questions.st: Broadcom Hardware Test Intern Rancho San Diego Ca interview
questions.a: A pull-up resistor ties a line weakly to VDD so it has a defined high level when nothing drives it, for example a floating input, a button, or an open-drain or open-collector bus such as I2C, where devices only pull low. Its value trades rise time (smaller is faster) against current and power when the line is pulled low.

questions.q: What is gate-level simulation used for?
questions.st: Broadcom Verification Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: Gate-level simulation runs the synthesized or post-layout netlist, often with SDF timing back-annotated. It catches synthesis-simulation mismatches, X-propagation and reset problems that RTL hides, scan and DFT behaviour, timing issues on paths that STA was told to ignore (false or multicycle paths, asynchronous logic), and power-up sequences, and it gives switching activity for power analysis.

questions.q: What is the difference between continuous and procedural assignments?
questions.st: Broadcom Verification Engineer Intern San Diego Ca interview
questions.a: Continuous assignments (assign y = a & b;) drive a net all the time: whenever a right-hand side changes, the net updates; they model combinational logic and wires. Procedural assignments happen inside always or initial blocks when that code executes, and assign to variables (reg or logic), which keep their value until assigned again. Procedural assignments can be blocking (=) or non-blocking (<=) and can model both combinational and sequential logic.

questions.q: How does SystemVerilog differ from Verilog?

For verification: classes and OOP, constrained random generation, functional coverage (covergroups), assertions (SVA), dynamic and associative arrays and queues, mailboxes and semaphores, fork-join variants, and clocking blocks. It is the base of UVM.

questions.q: Explain the operating regions of a MOSFET, and how transistors are used in analog versus digital circuits.
questions.st: Cadence Digital Hardware Intern Bangalore Rural Karnataka interview
questions.a: Cut-off (VGS < Vt): no channel, the transistor is off. Linear or triode (VGS > Vt and VDS < VGS - Vt): it acts like a voltage-controlled resistor. Saturation (VDS > VGS - Vt): the current depends mainly on VGS, so it acts as a current source. Digital circuits use the transistor as a switch, moving between cut-off and linear. Analog circuits bias it in saturation, where it gives gain (amplifiers, current mirrors, differential pairs).

questions.q: For a diode circuit with Vd = 0.7 V and RC = 1 us, draw Vr versus Vi.
questions.st: Cadence analog interview written questions 2020
questions.a: Without the figure, the common case is a diode clipper or peak detector. For a series diode with R and C forming a peak detector: when Vi exceeds Vr + 0.7 V the diode conducts and Vr follows Vi - 0.7 V; when Vi falls, the diode turns off and the capacitor holds Vr, decaying with time constant RC = 1 us. For a shunt clipper, Vr follows Vi until it reaches 0.7 V (plus any reference) and then stays clamped. Sketch the transfer curve with the 0.7 V breakpoints.

questions.q: With a sine wave on an inverter's input, in which region does each PMOS and NMOS operate across the cycle?
questions.st: Cadence Product Validation Engineer Noida Uttar Pradesh interview
questions.a: As the sine rises from 0: near 0 V the NMOS is off and the PMOS is in its linear region (output high). As Vin passes Vtn the NMOS turns on in saturation while the PMOS is still linear. Around the switching threshold both are saturated. Then the NMOS moves into linear and the PMOS into saturation, and above VDD - |Vtp| the PMOS turns off with the NMOS linear (output low). On the falling half the sequence reverses.

questions.q: What is instruction pipelining?
questions.st: Cadence Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: Instruction pipelining divides instruction execution into stages (fetch, decode, execute, memory access, write-back) with registers between them, so while one instruction executes, the next is being decoded and the one after is being fetched. Throughput approaches one instruction per cycle and the clock can be faster, although each instruction's latency stays the same; hazards need forwarding, stalls and branch prediction.

questions.q: C1 holds 1 C of charge at 1 V; C2 is an uncharged 1 F capacitor. When the switch between them closes through resistor R, how much energy is dissipated in R?
questions.st: Cadence analog interview written questions 2020
questions.a: Charge is conserved: the 1 C shares between two 1 F capacitors, so each ends at 0.5 V. The initial energy is 0.5 x 1 x 1^2 = 0.5 J; the final energy is 2 x 0.5 x 1 x 0.5^2 = 0.25 J. So 0.25 J, half of the initial energy, is dissipated in R, whatever the value of R (R only changes how fast it happens).

questions.q: Draw a circuit that generates the repeating 2-bit sequences 11, 01, 10, 11 and 00, 10, 01, 00.
questions.st: Cadence analog interview written questions 2020

questions.q: Explain false paths and half-cycle paths.
questions.st: Cadence Timing Engineer San Francisco California interview

A half-cycle path launches on one edge of the clock and captures on the opposite edge (for example a negative-edge flop feeding a positive-edge flop), so it only has half a period for setup, but more room for hold.

questions.q: Find the steady-state output across a parallel RC driven by Vi = Vp cos(t/RC).
questions.st: Cadence analog interview written questions 2020

questions.q: What are big-endian and little-endian?
questions.st: Cadence Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: They are the byte order of multi-byte words in memory. Big-endian stores the most significant byte at the lowest address (network order); little-endian stores the least significant byte first (x86, and most Arm systems). For 0x12345678 at address 0, big-endian memory holds 12 34 56 78 and little-endian holds 78 56 34 12. It matters when data crosses buses, files or networks.

questions.q: What are parasitics? What is EM/IR, and why do they cause reliability problems?
questions.st: Cadence Product Validation Engineer Noida Uttar Pradesh interview
questions.a: Parasitics are the unwanted resistance, capacitance and inductance of wires and devices, extracted from the layout (SPEF) and added to timing and power analysis. EM (electromigration) is the gradual movement of metal atoms caused by high current density, which creates voids (opens) or hillocks (shorts) over time. IR drop is the voltage loss on the power grid due to its resistance. EM causes long-term wear-out failures; IR drop slows or breaks circuits; both are signed off with current-density and voltage-drop limits.

questions.q: What are the inputs to a timing engine?
questions.st: Cadence Timing Engineer San Francisco California interview

For multi-mode multi-corner analysis, a set of each per scenario.

questions.q: What are timing arcs?
questions.st: Cadence Timing Engineer San Francisco California interview
questions.a: A timing arc is a delay path inside a cell or a net from one pin to another, described in the Liberty library. Combinational arcs go from an input to an output (positive unate, negative unate or non-unate). Sequential arcs go from the clock pin to the output (clock-to-Q), and timing-check arcs describe setup, hold, recovery and removal between data and clock. Net arcs connect a driver to its loads. STA traces paths by chaining arcs.

questions.q: Explain inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction in SystemVerilog.
questions.st: Cadence Design Verification Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: Inheritance: a class extends a base class and reuses its properties and methods (class burst_txn extends txn). Polymorphism: a base-class handle can point to a derived object, and virtual methods run the derived version at run time, so generic code works with any derived type. Abstraction: virtual classes and pure virtual methods define an interface that derived classes must implement, hiding implementation details. These are the basis of reusable testbenches and UVM.

questions.q: Explain the SystemVerilog event scheduler regions.
questions.st: Cadence Validation Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: Each time step is divided into regions. Preponed: values are sampled for assertions. Active: blocking assignments, continuous assignments and $display run. Inactive: #0 events. NBA: non-blocking assignments update. Observed: assertions are evaluated. Reactive: program blocks and assertion action blocks run. Postponed: $strobe and $monitor print final values. This ordering, with sampling before changes, is what lets clocking blocks and assertions avoid races with the design.

questions.q: Explain the UVM phases and why each matters.
questions.st: Cadence Design Verification Intern Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: Build phases run first: build_phase (top-down: create components and get config), connect_phase (bottom-up: connect TLM ports), end_of_elaboration_phase (check topology), start_of_simulation_phase. Then run_phase, which is a task and consumes time (in parallel with the run-time sub-phases reset, configure, main and shutdown). Cleanup phases follow: extract_phase, check_phase, report_phase, final_phase. Phasing makes every component build, connect, run and report in a consistent order; objections control when run_phase ends.

questions.q: What are the UVM phases and their properties?
questions.st: Cadence Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: Function phases take no simulation time: build (top-down), connect, end_of_elaboration, start_of_simulation, extract, check, report and final (bottom-up). Task phases consume time: run_phase, and the run-time sub-phases pre_reset, reset, configure, main and shutdown with pre and post variants, which run in parallel with run_phase. A phase ends when all raised objections are dropped. Build is top-down so parents create children; the others are bottom-up.

questions.q: What are the factory override methods in UVM?
questions.st: Cadence Verification Engineer New Delhi Delhi interview
questions.a: Type overrides replace every instance of a type: set_type_override_by_type(orig::get_type(), new::get_type()) or set_type_override_by_name(). Instance overrides replace only the objects created at a given hierarchy path: set_inst_override_by_type(path, orig::get_type(), new::get_type()) or by name. They only take effect for objects created with type_id::create() and must be set before the build_phase creates them. Instance overrides take priority over type overrides.

questions.q: Design an SRAM cell and explain how it works.
questions.st: Cisco Asic Design Engineer San Jose Ca interview
questions.a: The standard 6T SRAM cell is two cross-coupled inverters that hold a bit and its complement, plus two NMOS access transistors connecting the storage nodes to the bit lines BL and BLB, controlled by the word line. To read, precharge both bit lines high and raise the word line; the side storing 0 slowly discharges its bit line and a sense amplifier detects the small difference. To write, drive BL and BLB to opposite values and raise the word line; the strong drivers overpower the cell. Sizing matters: the pull-down must be stronger than the access transistor for read stability, and the access transistor stronger than the pull-up for writability.

questions.q: What is the difference between SRAM and DRAM?
questions.st: Cisco Hardware Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: SRAM stores each bit in a 6-transistor latch: fast, no refresh, compatible with the logic process, but large (low density) and costly; it is used for caches and register files. DRAM stores each bit as charge on a capacitor with one access transistor (1T1C): very dense and cheap per bit, but slower, reads are destructive, and the charge leaks so it must be refreshed every few tens of milliseconds; it is used for main memory and needs a special process.

questions.q: What is the difference between a microcontroller and a microprocessor? Describe the 8051 architecture.
questions.st: Cisco Hardware Engineer Manipal interview
questions.a: A microprocessor is a CPU on a chip that needs external memory and peripherals; a microcontroller integrates the CPU with program memory (ROM or flash), RAM, timers, serial ports and GPIO on one chip for embedded control. The 8051 is an 8-bit microcontroller with an 8-bit ALU and accumulator, 4 KB of on-chip ROM, 128 bytes of RAM including four register banks, 4 parallel I/O ports (P0 to P3), two 16-bit timers or counters, a full-duplex UART, 5 interrupt sources, a 16-bit program counter and data pointer, and a Harvard memory organisation.

questions.q: Explain RC and RL filters.
questions.st: Cisco Asic Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: An RC low-pass filter has R in series and C to ground: the capacitor shorts high frequencies, so the cut-off is fc = 1/(2 pi R C) with -20 dB/decade roll-off. Swapping them (C in series, R to ground) makes a high-pass filter. An RL filter does the same with an inductor, whose impedance rises with frequency: R in series with L to ground is a high-pass, L in series with R to ground is a low-pass, with fc = R/(2 pi L). Both are first-order filters with a 45 degree phase shift at fc.

questions.q: How do you multiply binary numbers?
questions.st: Cisco Hardware Intern United States interview
questions.a: Like long multiplication in decimal, but each partial product is either 0 or the multiplicand shifted: for each 1 bit of the multiplier, add the multiplicand shifted left by that bit's position. For example 101 x 11 = 101 + 1010 = 1111 (5 x 3 = 15). In hardware this is an array multiplier (AND gates for partial products plus adders), a sequential shift-and-add multiplier, or a fast Wallace or Dadda tree with Booth encoding to reduce the number of partial products. For signed numbers use Booth or sign extension.

questions.q: Walk through the complete ASIC flow.
questions.st: Cisco Asic Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: Specification and architecture, micro-architecture, RTL coding, functional verification (simulation, formal, emulation), lint, CDC and RDC checks, then synthesis with constraints into a netlist, DFT insertion (scan, MBIST), and logical equivalence checking. Physical design: floorplan and power grid, placement, clock tree synthesis, routing, with timing optimisation at each step. Sign-off: STA across corners and modes, IR drop and EM, signal integrity, physical verification (DRC, LVS, antenna, density), and final equivalence. Then tape-out of GDSII, fabrication, packaging, post-silicon validation and production test.

questions.q: What is an RLC network? Explain its components.
questions.st: Cisco Hardware Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: An RLC network combines a resistor (dissipates energy, V = IR), an inductor (stores energy in a magnetic field, V = L di/dt, impedance j omega L) and a capacitor (stores energy in an electric field, I = C dV/dt, impedance 1/(j omega C)). Together they form a second-order system with a resonant frequency f0 = 1/(2 pi sqrt(LC)) where the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, and a damping set by R and the quality factor Q. They are used in filters, tuned circuits and oscillators, and model power delivery networks and transmission lines.

questions.q: What is skin effect, and how does it affect PCB design?
questions.st: Cisco Senior Hardware Engineer United States interview
questions.a: At high frequencies, alternating current crowds toward the surface of a conductor, flowing in a layer whose depth decreases with the square root of frequency (about 2 um in copper at 1 GHz). The effective cross-section shrinks, so the resistance and loss of PCB traces rise with frequency, attenuating fast signals and degrading the eye. Designers use wider traces, smoother copper, low-loss dielectrics, shorter routes and equalisation in the SerDes to compensate.

questions.q: What is the difference between DRC and LVS?
questions.st: Cisco Asic Engineer I United States interview

LVS (layout versus schematic) extracts the circuit from the layout and checks that it matches the netlist: same devices, connections and sizes, with no shorts or opens. DRC makes the chip manufacturable; LVS makes sure what is manufactured is the intended circuit.

questions.st: Hudson River Trading Hardware Engineer Internship New York Ny interview
questions.a: Synthesis turns the HDL into a netlist of FPGA primitives: it infers logic, optimises it, and maps it to LUTs, flip-flops, carry chains, block RAMs and DSP slices. Implementation then places those primitives onto specific sites in the device, routes the connections through the programmable interconnect, runs timing analysis against the constraints, and finally generates the bitstream that configures the FPGA.

questions.q: Which physical CMOS parameters affect propagation delay?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hughes)
questions.a: Supply voltage (higher VDD is faster), threshold voltage (lower Vt is faster but leaks more), transistor width and length (wider and shorter is faster), gate oxide thickness and carrier mobility, load capacitance (fan-out, wire and diffusion capacitance), input slew, temperature, and process variation. Delay is roughly C VDD / I_on, so anything that increases drive current or reduces capacitance speeds the gate up.

questions.q: Explain the function of a muxed (scan) flip-flop.
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hughes)
questions.a: A muxed scan flip-flop is a normal D flip-flop with a 2:1 multiplexer on its D input. When scan enable (SE) is 0, the mux passes the functional data D, so the flop works normally and captures the circuit's response. When SE is 1, it passes the scan input SI from the previous flop's output, so all scan flops form a shift register (a scan chain) to load test patterns and unload results. It costs a mux delay on the data path.

questions.q: In equivalence checking, how do you handle the scan-enable signal?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hughes)
questions.a: Constrain it. When comparing RTL (without scan) against a scan-inserted netlist, set scan enable to its functional value (0) with a constant constraint, so the scan muxes always select functional data and the extra scan path does not appear as a difference. Similarly tie test-mode signals to functional values, and give the tool any scan-chain reordering information so register mapping works.

questions.q: How does PVT affect delay?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hughes)
questions.a: Process: fast corners (FF) have stronger transistors and shorter delay, slow corners (SS) longer delay. Voltage: a higher supply increases drive current and reduces delay. Temperature: in older nodes delay increases with temperature (lower mobility); in advanced nodes at low voltage, temperature inversion can make cold the slower corner because Vt rises. STA therefore checks setup at the slow corner and hold at the fast corner, plus on-chip variation derates.

questions.q: What are the components of power dissipation, and how do you reduce them?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hughes)
questions.a: Dynamic switching power alpha C V^2 f, from charging and discharging capacitances: reduce it with clock gating, lower voltage and frequency, less switching activity and smaller capacitance. Short-circuit power during transitions when both networks conduct: keep input slews sharp. Static leakage power (subthreshold, gate and junction leakage): reduce it with high-Vt cells, power gating, body biasing and lower supply. Voltage is the strongest lever because of the V^2 term.

questions.q: Explain the basic architecture of a microcontroller and how it differs from a microprocessor.
questions.st: Infineon Technologies interview experience (on-campus) 2023
questions.a: A microcontroller combines a CPU core with on-chip program memory (flash or ROM), data RAM, timers, ADCs, serial interfaces (UART, SPI, I2C), GPIO, an interrupt controller and a clock system on one chip, designed for embedded control at low cost and power. A microprocessor contains mainly the CPU (and caches) and relies on external memory and peripheral chips, optimised for high performance general computing.

questions.q: Why build a 16-bit microcontroller instead of cascading 8-bit ones?
questions.st: Infineon Technologies interview experience (on-campus) 2023
questions.a: A native 16-bit core processes 16-bit data in one instruction instead of several (cascading 8-bit operations needs carries between them and more instructions), addresses more memory directly, and gives better code density and performance per clock. Cascading two 8-bit parts adds glue logic, synchronisation and software complexity, and costs more board area and power than one integrated 16-bit device.

questions.q: Explain the keywords volatile, const and static in Embedded C.
questions.st: Infineon Technologies interview experience (on-campus) 2023
questions.a: volatile tells the compiler a variable can change outside the program's control (hardware registers, ISR-shared variables), so it must reread it on every access and not optimise reads or writes away. const makes a variable read-only, so the compiler can place it in flash and catch accidental writes. static inside a function keeps the variable's value between calls; at file scope it limits visibility to that file (internal linkage).

questions.q: What is the difference between Von Neumann and Harvard architectures? Give a practical use for each.
questions.st: Infineon Technologies interview experience (on-campus) 2023
questions.a: Von Neumann uses one memory and one bus for both instructions and data: simpler and flexible (programs can be loaded as data), but instruction and data accesses compete for the bus (the Von Neumann bottleneck); typical of general-purpose computers. Harvard uses separate memories and buses, so an instruction fetch and a data access happen at the same time: faster and common in DSPs and microcontrollers such as the 8051 and AVR. Modern CPUs are modified Harvard: split L1 caches over a unified memory.

questions.q: Explain the 5-stage pipeline, the types of hazards and data hazards, and how you would go beyond 5 stages.
questions.st: Intel Verification Engineer Folsom California interview
questions.a: The five stages are fetch, decode, execute, memory and write-back. Hazards: structural (shared resources), data (RAW, plus WAR and WAW in out-of-order designs) and control (branches). RAW data hazards are fixed by forwarding from the EX/MEM and MEM/WB registers, with a one-cycle stall for a load followed by a use. To go beyond five stages, split the slow stages (cache access, decode, multiply) into more stages for a higher clock (superpipelining), and add better branch prediction because the mispredict penalty grows, or go superscalar and out of order.

questions.st: Intel Design Verification Engineer United States interview
questions.a: Build a reference memory model and a coherence-aware scoreboard that knows the ordering rules, with agents on every master port and on the memory side. Drive random traffic from all masters concurrently, aimed at a small set of addresses to force sharing, evictions and conflicts, plus directed tests for fills, write-backs, coherence transitions, snoops and races. Add assertions on protocol and invariants (for example a single writable copy), check data on every read against the model, and close coverage on cache states, transitions crossed with masters, and hit or miss at each level.

questions.q: What are a cache and a TLB?
questions.st: Intel interview experience, set 4 (on-campus, full time)
questions.a: A cache is a small, fast memory that keeps copies of recently used data and instructions close to the processor, so most accesses avoid slow main memory. A TLB (translation lookaside buffer) is a small cache of virtual-to-physical address translations from the page tables, so most memory accesses do not need a page table walk. Both rely on locality; a TLB miss costs a page walk, a cache miss costs a trip to the next memory level.

questions.q: What is virtual memory?
questions.st: Intel interview experience, set 4 (on-campus, full time)
questions.a: Virtual memory is an abstraction in which each program sees its own large, private address space. The hardware MMU translates virtual addresses to physical memory in pages using page tables set up by the operating system; pages not in memory can live on disk and are loaded on a page fault. It gives isolation, protection, flexible allocation and the ability to run programs larger than physical memory.

questions.q: How is a flip-flop replaced with a scan flip-flop?

The tool then stitches the flops into chains by connecting each Q (or a dedicated SO) to the next flop's SI, connects SE and the scan ports to top-level pins, inserts lockup latches between clock domains, and verifies the chains with DRC.

questions.q: Add two numbers without using the +, -, * or / operators.
questions.st: Intel Validation Engineer Israel interview
questions.a: Use bitwise logic as a hardware adder does: XOR gives the sum without carries and AND shifted left gives the carries. Repeat until there are no carries: while (b != 0) { carry = (a & b) << 1; a = a ^ b; b = carry; } return a;. This loop takes at most as many iterations as there are bits.

questions.q: Build circuits using decoders and multiplexers.
questions.st: Intel Cpu Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: A decoder with n inputs produces all 2^n minterms, so any function of those inputs is an OR of the selected decoder outputs (for example a full adder from a 3-to-8 decoder and two OR gates). A 2^n:1 multiplexer can implement any n-variable function by tying its data inputs to the truth table values, or any (n+1)-variable function by using the last variable, its complement or constants as data inputs. Larger muxes and decoders are built by cascading smaller ones.

questions.q: Compare RISC and CISC instruction sets, with the pros and cons of each.
questions.st: Intel Cpu Verification Engineer Austin Texas interview
questions.a: RISC (Arm, RISC-V, MIPS) uses a small set of simple, fixed-length instructions, load-store memory access and many registers: easy to decode and pipeline, low power, but more instructions per program. CISC (x86) has many complex, variable-length instructions with memory operands: compact code and fewer instructions, but complex decode; modern x86 cores translate them into RISC-like micro-ops internally. Today the difference is mostly in decode and ecosystem rather than performance.

The synthesis tool adds the estimated wire capacitance to the pin loads and computes cell delay from the library tables with that load. WLMs are inaccurate in deep submicron designs, so physical synthesis or topographical mode is used instead.

questions.q: What factors improve the propagation delay of a standard cell?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Intel)
questions.a: Higher drive strength (wider transistors), lower threshold voltage cells, higher supply voltage, lower load capacitance (fewer fan-outs, shorter wires), sharper input slew, fewer series transistors (prefer NAND to NOR, avoid tall stacks), a smaller internal parasitic capacitance through good layout, and logic restructuring to reduce logic depth. Each comes with area, power or leakage costs.

questions.q: What is RAM, and what types of RAM are there?
questions.st: Intel Dft Engineer California Md interview
questions.a: RAM (random access memory) can be read and written at any address in roughly the same time and is usually volatile. The main types are SRAM (static, 6T latches, fast, used for caches and registers) and DRAM (dynamic, capacitor cells needing refresh, dense, used for main memory, in variants such as DDR, LPDDR, GDDR and HBM). Non-volatile random-access variants include MRAM, FRAM and ReRAM. On chip there are single-port, dual-port and register-file memories.

questions.q: What is a pull-up? What is high impedance?
questions.st: Intel Fpga Intern Gdansk interview
questions.a: A pull-up is a resistor (or weak transistor) to VDD that gives a line a default high level when no device drives it, used on open-drain buses and floating inputs. High impedance (Z) is the state of an output that is not driving at all, with both transistors off, so it neither sources nor sinks current and another device can drive the line; it is the third state of a tri-state buffer.

questions.q: What is the difference between a MOSFET and a BJT?
questions.st: Intel Post Si Validation Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: A MOSFET is voltage-controlled: the gate voltage sets the channel conductance, with almost no DC gate current, so it has very high input impedance, low static power and dense integration, which is why it dominates digital logic. A BJT is current-controlled: a small base current controls a larger collector current; it has higher transconductance, better matching and higher gain per current, and is used in analog, RF and high-current applications, but it draws base current and is less dense.

questions.q: Why are power stripes routed in the top metal layers?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Intel)
questions.a: The top metal layers are the thickest and widest, so they have the lowest resistance, which minimises IR drop and electromigration for high power currents. Putting the global power grid there also leaves the lower, finer layers free for dense signal routing, and the top layers connect directly to the bumps or pads. Power then reaches cells through via stacks down to the standard cell rails.

questions.q: Write assembly that leaves r3 = r1 * r2, using as many registers as you like.
questions.st: Intel Cpu Validation Engineer Haifa interview
questions.a: Use shift-and-add (generic RISC syntax): r3 = 0; loop: if the low bit of r2 is 1, add r1 to r3; shift r1 left by one; shift r2 right by one; repeat while r2 is not 0. For example: mov r3, #0; loop: and r4, r2, #1; cmp r4, #0; beq skip; add r3, r3, r1; skip: lsl r1, r1, #1; lsr r2, r2, #1; cmp r2, #0; bne loop. A simpler but slower version adds r1 to r3 r2 times.

questions.q: How do you fix timing violations on latch-to-latch paths?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Intel)
questions.a: Latch-to-latch paths can use time borrowing: a slow stage can borrow time from the next phase, as long as the data arrives before the latch closes. To fix a real violation, reduce the logic delay (faster cells, restructuring, moving logic across the latch boundary), adjust the clock phases or duty cycle, or retime so each phase has a balanced amount of logic. Check that borrowing does not hide a violation in the following stage, and fix hold with delay buffers.

questions.q: Describe the UVM phases. What is the difference between run_phase and main_phase?
questions.st: Intel Sr Verification Engineer United States interview
questions.a: UVM phases: build, connect, end_of_elaboration and start_of_simulation (functions), run_phase (a task), then extract, check, report and final. run_phase is a single task that runs for the whole simulation in every component. main_phase is one of the run-time sub-phases (pre_reset, reset, configure, main, shutdown and their pre/post variants) that run in parallel with run_phase in order, so you can separate reset, configuration and traffic and even jump between phases. Most teams use run_phase only.

questions.q: What does the virtual keyword do in SystemVerilog?
questions.st: Intel Soc Verification Engineer San Jose Ca interview
questions.a: On a class method, virtual makes the call resolved by the object's actual type at run time (dynamic dispatch), so a derived class's override runs even through a base-class handle. virtual class declares an abstract class that cannot be instantiated. A virtual interface is a handle to an interface instance, which lets class-based testbench code access the DUT's signals.

questions.q: What formal verification issues have you faced, and how did you resolve them?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Intel)
questions.a: Typical issues: state-space explosion, so proofs do not converge (fixed with abstraction, cutting, smaller data widths and assume-guarantee); over-constrained assumptions hiding real behaviour (check with cover properties and vacuity checks); under-constrained inputs giving false counter-examples (add the right protocol assumptions); bounded proofs that are not deep enough; and reset and initial state handling. Describe one real example and how you fixed it.

questions.q: Why use the UVM methodology?
questions.st: Intel Sr Verification Engineer Santa Clara Ca interview
questions.a: UVM provides a standard, reusable structure for testbenches: components, phases, the factory for overriding, config_db for configuration, sequences for stimulus, TLM for communication, and reporting. Teams and vendors share the same methodology, so verification IP plugs in, environments are reused from block to SoC level, and constrained-random coverage-driven verification scales. The cost is boilerplate and a learning curve.

questions.q: Write a BCD converter in Verilog.
questions.st: Intel Hardware Intern Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: A binary-to-BCD converter is usually written with the double-dabble (shift-and-add-3) algorithm: shift the binary number left one bit at a time into BCD digits, and before each shift add 3 to any BCD digit that is 5 or more. questions.q: How do AND and OR gates work, and how are they built in CMOS?
questions.st: Marvell Hardware Engineer United States interview
questions.a: In CMOS the natural gates are inverting: NAND has parallel PMOS to VDD and series NMOS to ground; NOR has series PMOS and parallel NMOS. An AND gate is built as a NAND followed by an inverter, and an OR gate as a NOR followed by an inverter, so each takes 6 transistors and an extra stage of delay. That is why logic is usually expressed with NAND and NOR.

questions.q: Explain RAW, WAW and WAR hazards and how in-order and out-of-order pipelines handle them.
questions.st: Marvell Asic Design Engineer Santa Clara California interview
questions.a: RAW (read after write) is a true dependency: the reader must get the producer's value; in-order pipelines use forwarding and stalls, out-of-order cores wait in reservation stations until the tag is broadcast. WAR (write after read) and WAW (write after write) are name dependencies from register reuse; in-order pipelines that write back in order do not see them, while out-of-order cores remove them with register renaming, and the reorder buffer keeps the final state in program order.

A reference model with random traffic and coverage completes it.

questions.q: How are structural hazards handled in out-of-order pipelines?
questions.st: Marvell Asic Design Engineer Santa Clara California interview
questions.a: Through resource arbitration in the scheduler: instructions only issue when a free functional unit (and a result bus slot) is available, otherwise they wait in their reservation station or issue queue. Designers add multiple copies of busy units, pipeline the units so a new operation can start every cycle, and use separate ports for loads and stores. Full queues (ROB, load and store queues, physical registers) stall dispatch.

questions.q: How do you balance pipeline stages to meet a target clock period?
questions.st: Marvell Design Verification Engineer Santa Clara California interview
questions.a: Measure the delay of each stage, then move logic from the longest stage into neighbouring ones (retiming), split the slowest stage by adding a register, or duplicate logic so it can be computed in parallel. The clock period must be at least the slowest stage plus register overhead (clock-to-Q and setup) and skew, so the goal is equal stage delays. Synthesis tools can retime automatically; check that latency and hazards are still handled.

questions.q: How many address lines does a given memory need?
questions.st: Marvell Design Verification Intern Austin Texas interview
questions.a: Address lines = log2(number of addressable locations). For a memory of 2^n words you need n lines: 1 K words need 10, 64 K need 16, 1 M need 20. If the memory is byte-addressed but organised in wider words, the lowest bits select the byte within the word. For example a 32 KB memory with 32-bit words has 8 K words, so 13 word-address lines.

questions.q: Given an anti-aliasing filter response with a bump before roll-off, what are the two main reasons to put it before an ADC?
questions.st: Marvell Hardware Engineer San Jose California interview
questions.a: First, to remove signal and noise above the Nyquist frequency (half the sample rate), which would otherwise alias into the band of interest and cannot be removed afterwards. Second, to limit the noise bandwidth, so out-of-band noise and interferers do not raise the noise floor. The bump (peaking) before roll-off comes from a high-Q filter that gives a sharper transition, at the cost of some ripple and phase distortion in the passband.

questions.q: How does time-division multiplexing work, and what are its corner cases?
questions.st: Marvell Design Verification Engineer interview
questions.a: Time-division multiplexing shares one link among several streams by giving each a time slot in a repeating frame; faster streams get more slots, and the receiver uses a frame sync to know which slot belongs to which stream. Corner cases: frame alignment and loss of sync, streams whose rates do not divide the frame evenly (needing stuffing bits), all slots used versus idle slots, clock drift between sources (buffers and slips), and reconfiguring the slot allocation without corrupting data.

questions.q: How would you implement a circular buffer in C?
questions.st: Marvell Hardware Validation United States interview
questions.a: Use an array, a head index for reads and a tail index for writes, and a count (or keep one slot empty to tell full from empty). Push: if not full, buf[tail] = x; tail = (tail + 1) % N; count++. Pop: if not empty, x = buf[head]; head = (head + 1) % N; count--. With N a power of two, use & (N - 1) instead of %. For a producer and a consumer in an ISR, make the indexes volatile and update each from one side only.

questions.q: What is X-propagation, and why does it happen? Give an example.
questions.st: Marvell Hardware Engineer United States interview
questions.a: X-propagation is how unknown values spread through a design in simulation. It happens when a register has no reset, when there are multiple conflicting drivers, out-of-range array indexes, uninitialised memories or power-down corruption. For example, an if (sel) statement with sel = X takes the else branch in RTL (X optimism) and hides the bug, while the gate-level netlist propagates X (or real hardware picks a random value). Use resets, X-checking assertions and X-propagation simulation modes to find it.

questions.q: What is the difference between ASIC and FPGA design?
questions.st: Marvell Asic Design Engineer interview
questions.a: ASIC design produces a custom chip: you control every gate and wire, so it gives the best performance, power and area, but needs physical design, sign-off and fabrication (high NRE, months of turnaround, no fixes after tape-out). FPGA design maps the logic onto a prefabricated reconfigurable device (LUTs, flops, block RAM, DSPs): fast to iterate and reprogrammable, but slower, more power hungry and more expensive per unit. Coding and timing closure also differ (FPGA-specific primitives, no custom clock trees).

questions.q: What is the transfer function of a simple VCO?
questions.st: Marvell Design Verification Engineer San Jose California interview
questions.a: A VCO's output frequency is linear in its control voltage: f = f0 + Kvco Vc. Phase is the integral of frequency, so in a PLL model the VCO's transfer function from control voltage to output phase is phi(s) / Vc(s) = Kvco / s: an integrator, which adds a pole at the origin to the loop.

questions.q: What is time borrowing in latches?
questions.st: Marvell Asic Engineer San Jose California interview
questions.a: A latch is transparent for a whole clock phase, so if the logic before it is slow, data can arrive after the opening edge and still be captured before the latch closes. That stage borrows time from the next stage, which then has less time. It lets latch-based designs balance uneven logic across stages, and STA tools compute the borrowed amount and check the next stage.

questions.q: Which metal layers are used for power and clock?
questions.st: Marvell Asic Design Engineer interview
questions.a: The top, thickest metal layers carry the global power grid and often the main clock spines, because they have the lowest resistance (less IR drop and better electromigration margin) and the clock benefits from low RC delay. Lower and mid layers handle local signal routing. Exactly which layers depends on the technology's metal stack.

questions.q: With 2 masters and 4 slaves on a bus, what properties would you write to check it?

Write these as SVA with cover properties for each master-slave pair.

questions.q: Explain Tomasulo's out-of-order algorithm in depth.
questions.st: Marvell Asic Design Engineer Santa Clara California interview
questions.a: Tomasulo's algorithm issues instructions in order to reservation stations. When an instruction issues, it reads available operands or records the tag of the reservation station that will produce each missing one; the register status table marks the destination register with the new tag (renaming), removing WAR and WAW hazards. Stations monitor the common data bus: when a producer finishes, it broadcasts tag and value, and all waiting stations and registers with that tag capture it. Instructions execute when their operands are ready, so they can complete out of order; a reorder buffer is added for in-order commit, precise exceptions and speculation.

questions.st: Marvell Asic Design Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: The top module instantiates the DUT and interfaces, puts virtual interfaces into config_db, and calls run_test(). The test builds the environment, which builds agents (sequencer, driver, monitor), scoreboards and coverage. In connect_phase, drivers connect to sequencers and monitors to scoreboards through analysis ports. In run_phase, the test raises an objection and starts sequences; items go sequencer to driver to DUT pins; monitors observe and broadcast; scoreboards compare against a reference model; then objections drop, and check and report phases summarise the results.

questions.q: How do you know your testbench has covered all the cases?
questions.st: Marvell Asic Verification Engineer United States interview
questions.a: Measure it: functional coverage tied to the verification plan (every feature, corner case and cross of interesting conditions has a bin), code coverage (line, branch, condition, toggle and FSM) to find untested RTL, and assertion coverage to show properties were exercised non-vacuously. Review the holes, write targeted tests or constraints, and run regressions with many seeds until coverage closes and the bug rate drops. Coverage shows what was tested, not that the checks are right, so review the checkers too.

questions.q: How does a transaction pass from the generator to the driver in a SystemVerilog testbench?
questions.st: Marvell Design Verification Engineer San Jose California interview
questions.a: The generator (or sequence) creates and randomizes a transaction object and puts it into a mailbox shared with the driver; the driver blocks on mailbox.get(), converts the transaction into pin-level activity through the virtual interface, and may send back a completion through another mailbox or an event. In UVM, the same thing happens through start_item and finish_item on the sequencer and get_next_item and item_done in the driver.

questions.q: What are the UVM phases, and why are they used?
questions.st: Marvell Staff Design Verification Engineer United States interview
questions.a: UVM phases split the simulation into ordered steps that every component follows: build (create sub-components top-down), connect (hook up TLM ports), end_of_elaboration and start_of_simulation (checks and printing), run (the time-consuming test, optionally divided into reset, configure, main and shutdown), then extract, check, report and final. Phasing synchronises all components without manual coordination, and objections decide when the run phase ends.

questions.q: What data types does SystemVerilog have?
questions.st: Marvell Design Verification Intern Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: 2-state types: bit, byte, shortint, int, longint; 4-state types: logic, reg, wire, integer, time; real, shortreal and realtime; string; enum, struct and union (packed or unpacked); typedef; arrays: packed and unpacked fixed-size arrays, dynamic arrays, associative arrays and queues; classes, events, mailboxes, semaphores, chandle and virtual interfaces.

questions.q: Why SystemVerilog? How does Verilog differ from C?
questions.st: Marvell Design Verification Intern Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: SystemVerilog adds what Verilog lacks for large designs and testbenches: classes and OOP, constrained random generation, functional coverage, assertions, interfaces, packages, richer types and always_ff and always_comb for design intent. Verilog differs from C because it describes hardware: everything runs concurrently, there is a notion of time and of clocks, 4-state values (X and Z), and blocking versus non-blocking assignments; C is a sequential program executed instruction by instruction.

questions.q: What is the difference between Verilog tasks and functions?
questions.st: Marvell Asic Design Engineer Santa Clara California interview
questions.a: A function returns a value, executes in zero time, cannot contain delays or event controls, cannot call tasks, and needs at least one input; it models combinational calculations. A task can have any number of inputs and outputs, can contain delays, @ and wait (so it can consume simulation time), can call other tasks and functions, and does not return a value directly. Use functions for computations, tasks for timed stimulus.

questions.q: What is the difference between inter-statement and intra-statement delays in Verilog?
questions.st: Marvell Design Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: An inter-statement (regular) delay, #5 a = b;, waits 5 time units and then evaluates b and assigns it, so it samples b late. An intra-statement delay, a = #5 b;, evaluates b now, waits 5 time units, then assigns the saved value, so it models a transport delay of the value sampled at that moment. With non-blocking assignments, a <= #5 b; schedules the update 5 units later without blocking the process.

questions.q: What is the total power dissipation of a CMOS circuit with load capacitance C at frequency F?
questions.st: MaxLinear interview questions 2020 (Digital Design Engineer written test)
questions.a: Dynamic power P = alpha C V^2 F, where alpha is the switching activity (the fraction of cycles the node switches, 1 for a clock). The total also includes short-circuit power during transitions and static leakage power: P_total = alpha C V^2 F + P_short-circuit + V I_leak.

questions.q: Which CMOS gate is faster, NAND or AND?
questions.st: MaxLinear interview questions 2020 (Digital Design Engineer written test)
questions.a: NAND is faster. In CMOS a NAND is a single inverting stage, while an AND gate is a NAND followed by an inverter, which adds a stage of delay (and area). A NAND is also usually faster than a NOR, because its series transistors are the faster NMOS while a NOR stacks the slower PMOS.

questions.q: Compute the Elmore delay of an RC tree with a branch.
questions.st: MaxLinear interview questions 2020 (Digital Design Engineer written test)
questions.a: For an RC tree, the Elmore delay to a node i is the sum over every capacitor k of C_k times the resistance shared between the path from the source to i and the path from the source to k: T_i = sum of R_ik C_k. For a branch, capacitors on the other branch only see the common resistance up to the branch point, while capacitors on the same path see their full upstream resistance. Write the shared resistance for each capacitor and add up the terms.

questions.q: Design a TDM system carrying 120 Mbps from streams of 10, 40 and 80 Mbps, working for any X, Y, Z with 10X + 40Y + 80Z = 120.
questions.st: MaxLinear interview questions 2020 (Digital Design Engineer written test)
questions.a: Use a frame of 12 slots, each carrying 10 Mbps, so 120 Mbps in total. A 10 Mbps stream takes 1 slot per frame, a 40 Mbps stream 4 slots and an 80 Mbps stream 8 slots; any combination with 10X + 40Y + 80Z = 120 fills exactly 12 slots. A slot-allocation table (programmed per configuration) tells the multiplexer which input to select in each slot, a counter steps through the slots, input FIFOs absorb the rate differences, and a frame-sync pattern lets the receiver demultiplex with the same table.

questions.q: Design a circuit that complements the input data when enable is on, and passes it unchanged otherwise.
questions.st: MaxLinear interview questions 2020 (Digital Design Engineer written test)
questions.a: Use an XOR gate per bit: out = data XOR enable. When enable = 1, XOR inverts each bit; when enable = 0, it passes the data unchanged. For a bus, replicate enable across the width: assign out = data ^ {N{en}};.

questions.q: Following that design, what changes are needed to compute Z = G * Y?
questions.st: MaxLinear interview questions 2020 (Digital Design Engineer written test)
questions.a: Multiplying Y by G adds a multiplier stage after the adder tree. At 300 MHz, a full multiplier will not fit in one cycle with slow adders, so pipeline it: split it into partial products and an adder tree across several register stages, or use a DSP block, and widen the registers to hold the product (width of G plus width of Y). Balance the pipeline so the extra latency is matched on any parallel paths.

questions.q: How many multipliers are needed to build a complex multiplier?
questions.st: MaxLinear interview questions 2020 (Digital Design Engineer written test)
questions.a: (a + jb)(c + jd) = (ac - bd) + j(ad + bc) needs 4 real multipliers and 2 adders directly. With Gauss's trick it needs only 3 multipliers: k1 = c(a + b), k2 = a(d - c), k3 = b(c + d); then real = k1 - k3 and imaginary = k1 + k2, at the cost of more additions.

questions.q: Implement an FIR filter with h0 = h4 and h1 = h2 using the minimum number of multipliers.
questions.st: MaxLinear interview questions 2020 (Digital Design Engineer written test)
questions.a: Use the symmetry to add before multiplying. y = h0 x[n] + h1 x[n-1] + h2 x[n-2] + h3 x[n-3] + h4 x[n-4], with h0 = h4 and h1 = h2, becomes y = h0 (x[n] + x[n-4]) + h1 (x[n-1] + x[n-2]) + h3 x[n-3], so it needs only 3 multipliers instead of 5, plus pre-adders. Linear-phase FIR filters are symmetric for exactly this reason.

questions.a: With a 1 MHz clock, 5 seconds is 5,000,000 cycles, so use a 23-bit counter (2^23 = 8.4 million). When the car is turned off, clear the counter and start counting; keep the headlights on while the count is below 4,999,999; turn them off when it reaches that value, and stop counting. If the car is turned on again, reset the counter and keep the lights on. A small FSM with states ON, COUNTING and OFF handles it, and the car-off input should be synchronised and debounced.

questions.q: Define a depletion-mode MOS device.
questions.st: MediaTek interview questions and experience
questions.a: A depletion-mode MOSFET has a channel already present at zero gate voltage, created by implanting dopants under the gate, so it conducts at VGS = 0 and its threshold voltage is negative (for NMOS). Applying a negative gate voltage depletes the channel and turns it off, while a positive voltage enhances it. They were used as loads in NMOS logic and are used in some analog and power circuits.

questions.q: What is the difference between a microprocessor and a microcontroller?
questions.st: MediaTek interview questions and experience
questions.a: A microprocessor is a general-purpose CPU that relies on external memory, storage and peripheral chips; it is designed for high performance and runs a full operating system. A microcontroller integrates a CPU with flash, RAM, timers, ADCs, communication peripherals and GPIO on one chip; it is designed for dedicated embedded control at low cost and low power.

questions.q: A right shift and a left shift are equivalent to which arithmetic operations?

For signed numbers, an arithmetic right shift (copying the sign bit) divides by 2^n, rounding toward negative infinity.

questions.q: Can you measure a 1 GHz square wave with a 1 GHz oscilloscope and probe? What will the waveform look like, and why?
questions.st: Meta Hardware Engineer Menlo Park California interview
questions.a: Not accurately. A 1 GHz square wave has its fundamental at 1 GHz plus odd harmonics at 3, 5 and 7 GHz. A 1 GHz scope (and probe) attenuates the fundamental by about 3 dB and removes the harmonics, so the trace looks like a sine wave of reduced amplitude with slow edges, and the rise time you see is the instrument's (about 0.35 / 1 GHz = 350 ps), not the signal's. Rule of thumb: use a bandwidth of 3 to 5 times the signal frequency, or 0.35 divided by the signal's rise time.

questions.q: Draw a simple NMOS current mirror. What are its drawbacks, and which topology overcomes them? What is its output swing?
questions.st: Micron Mixed Signal Verification Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: Two NMOS with gates tied together; M1 is diode-connected and carries Iref, so M2 sinks Iout = Iref (W/L)2/(W/L)1. Drawbacks: channel-length modulation makes Iout depend on M2's drain voltage (output resistance only ro), and mismatch causes errors. A cascode mirror (stacking transistors) or a Wilson mirror increases the output resistance by about gm ro and improves accuracy, at the cost of headroom. The output must stay above VGS - Vt (one overdrive) for the simple mirror, or about VGS + Vov for a cascode.

questions.q: Draw a two-stage CMOS amplifier. Derive its gain and output impedance, find its poles and zeros, and discuss stability and frequency compensation.
questions.st: Micron Mixed Signal Verification Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: Stage 1 is a differential pair with a current-mirror load (gain gm1 (ro2 || ro4)); stage 2 is a common-source amplifier with a current-source load (gain gm6 (ro6 || ro7)). Total DC gain is the product, often 60 to 80 dB, and the output impedance is ro6 || ro7. There are two main poles, one at each high-impedance node, so the amplifier needs compensation: a Miller capacitor Cc between the two stages splits the poles (pushing the first lower and the second higher) for about 60 degrees of phase margin. The Miller capacitor also creates a right-half-plane zero at gm6/Cc, cancelled with a series nulling resistor.

questions.q: Draw the supply current of an inverter over time as its input switches from low to high.
questions.st: Micron Design Verification Engineer Boise Idaho interview
questions.a: While the input is low, only leakage current flows. As the input rises past Vtn, both transistors conduct briefly, so a short-circuit current pulse flows from VDD to ground, peaking near the switching threshold. For a rising input the output falls, and the load capacitor discharges through the NMOS to ground, so that current is not drawn from VDD (the supply current is drawn on the opposite, falling-input transition, when the PMOS charges the load). Afterwards the current returns to leakage.

questions.q: For a single-ended CMOS differential amplifier, mark the inverting and non-inverting inputs and derive its gain, output resistance, poles and zeros.
questions.st: Micron Mixed Signal Verification Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: In a differential pair with a current-mirror load, the input transistor on the diode-connected side of the mirror is the non-inverting input (its current is mirrored to the output), and the transistor at the output node is the inverting input. Small-signal gain Av = gm1 (ro2 || ro4), and output resistance Rout = ro2 || ro4. The dominant pole is at the output, 1/(2 pi Rout CL); the mirror node gives a second, non-dominant pole near gm3/Cmirror, with a left-half-plane zero at about twice that frequency.

questions.q: Given a CMOS circuit, write its Boolean equation.
questions.st: Micron Dft Engineer Brazil interview
questions.a: Look at the pull-down network: series NMOS transistors mean AND, parallel means OR. Write the pull-down function, and the output is its complement (CMOS gates are inverting). For example, NMOS A in series with the parallel pair B and C gives F = NOT(A AND (B OR C)). Check that the pull-up network is the dual (parallel where the pull-down is series).

questions.q: Two capacitors charged to different voltages are connected through a transistor. What happens to the voltages when it turns on?
questions.st: Micron Design Verification Engineer Boise Idaho interview
questions.a: Charge flows from the higher-voltage capacitor to the lower one until both reach the same voltage, which is set by charge conservation: Vfinal = (C1 V1 + C2 V2) / (C1 + C2). Some energy is lost in the transistor's resistance (whatever its value). If the transistor is an NMOS whose gate is not high enough, it can stop conducting when the voltage reaches VG - Vt, so the voltages may not fully equalise. This is charge sharing, as in DRAM reads.

questions.q: Two inverters in a loop: what is the oscillation frequency, and how do you increase the period?
questions.st: Micron interview experience for Semiconductor Engineer (on-campus)
questions.a: It does not oscillate. Two inverters in a loop give non-inverting feedback, which is a bistable latch: it settles to one of two stable states and stays there (this is the core of an SRAM cell). An oscillator needs an odd number of inversions, such as a 3-stage ring oscillator with period 2 N td; to increase its period, add stages or load, or starve the current.
