questions.q: What sets the operating frequency of a microprocessor, and how many cycles does an instruction take?
questions.st: Micron interview experience for Semiconductor Engineer (on-campus)
questions.a: The clock frequency is set by the critical path (the slowest pipeline stage including register overhead), limited further by power and thermal budgets and the supply voltage. Cycles per instruction depend on the design: in an ideal pipeline one instruction completes every cycle (CPI = 1), superscalar cores complete several (CPI below 1), while stalls from cache misses, branch mispredicts and dependencies increase it. Older non-pipelined or microcoded CPUs took several cycles per instruction.

questions.q: Draw the MOSFET ID-VGS and ID-VDS characteristics.
questions.st: Micron Mixed Signal Verification Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: ID versus VGS: zero below Vt, then rising quadratically in saturation (ID = k/2 (VGS - Vt)^2), becoming more linear at high fields in short-channel devices, with a small exponential subthreshold current below Vt. ID versus VDS for several VGS values: rising roughly linearly in the triode region, bending over at VDS = VGS - Vt, and nearly flat in saturation with a slight upward slope from channel-length modulation; higher VGS gives higher curves.

questions.q: How do you pass a config_db setting from a lower level of the hierarchy to a higher one?
questions.st: Micron Senior Verification Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: config_db is meant to flow top-down, but any component can call set() with a context and path that a higher-level component will query. A lower component can do uvm_config_db #(T)::set(null, "uvm_test_top.env", "name", value), and the parent calls get() afterwards (after the child's build_phase, for example in connect_phase), because set and get are matched at run time. A cleaner way to pass information upward is through a TLM analysis port, a callback, or a shared configuration object handle.

Bias towards corners with dist (for example more weight on 0 and the maximum value), use inline randomize() with { } for specific tests, check that randomize() returns 1, and add functional coverage to confirm the bounds and corner values were actually hit.

questions.q: Is an LPDDR5 PHY backward compatible?
questions.st: Micron Asic Design Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: LPDDR5 itself is not backward compatible with LPDDR4 at the device level: it uses different clocking (a separate WCK data clock), voltages and protocol features. But many LPDDR5 controller and PHY IPs are designed as combo PHYs that support LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X as well (and LPDDR5X), switching modes in configuration. So the answer depends on the specific PHY: check its datasheet for supported standards.

questions.q: Print a binary tree in zig-zag order.
questions.st: Micron interview experience for Semiconductor Engineer (on-campus)
questions.a: Do a level-order (breadth-first) traversal with a queue, processing one level at a time, and keep a flag for the direction: collect each level's values in a list and reverse it on every other level before printing. A two-stack version avoids reversing: push children left-then-right for one direction and right-then-left for the other. Time O(n), space O(width of the tree).

questions.q: What is the difference between always and initial blocks?
questions.st: Micron Design Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: An initial block runs once, starting at time 0, and is used in testbenches for stimulus and setup (and on FPGAs for initial register values); synthesis otherwise ignores it. An always block runs repeatedly forever, re-triggered by its sensitivity list or timing controls; always @(posedge clk) describes flip-flops and always @(*) combinational logic, so it is the synthesizable construct for hardware.

questions.q: Write a sequence that sends 10 back-to-back read and write commands, where a read may never immediately follow a write.
questions.st: Micron Senior Verification Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview

The first item is unconstrained (it may be a write). Alternatively randomize an array of 10 commands at once with constraint foreach (c[i]) if (i > 0 && c[i-1] == WRITE) c[i] != READ;.

questions.q: What array types does SystemVerilog have?
questions.st: Micron Design Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: Packed arrays (bit [7:0] a) are a contiguous vector that can be used as a number. Unpacked fixed-size arrays (int a[8]) hold separate elements. Dynamic arrays (int a[]) are sized at run time with new[]. Associative arrays (int a[string] or a[int]) are sparse and indexed by any key, good for memory models. questions.q: How do you size the transistors of an inverter?
questions.st: NVIDIA ASIC Design Engineer interview, Hillsboro
questions.a: Size the PMOS wider than the NMOS to balance rise and fall delays, because hole mobility is about 2 to 3 times lower than electron mobility: typically Wp/Wn = 2 to 3 for equal drive and a switching threshold near VDD/2. Then scale both up together for the load: a larger inverter drives more capacitance faster but presents more input capacitance to the previous stage, so chains are sized with a constant fan-out of about 4 per stage (logical effort).

questions.q: What are the characteristics of CMOS?
questions.st: NVIDIA ASIC Design Engineer interview, Hillsboro
questions.a: Near-zero static power (only leakage, because no DC path exists in steady state), full rail-to-rail output swing, high noise margins, very high input impedance, inverting gates built from complementary pull-up and pull-down networks, delay set by charging load capacitance, and excellent scaling and density. Its main power cost is dynamic switching power, plus leakage in advanced nodes.

questions.q: Why is CMOS used to implement logic gates?
questions.st: NVIDIA ASIC Design Engineer interview
questions.a: CMOS gates draw almost no static current, give full logic levels and good noise margins, have very high input impedance so one gate can drive many others, and scale well to billions of transistors on a chip. The complementary networks make logic design regular (series and parallel transistors map to AND and OR), and the process is cheap and mature.

questions.q: Explain pipeline design and pipeline hazards.
questions.st: NVIDIA Asic Design Verification Engineer United States interview
questions.a: Pipeline design splits a long path into stages separated by registers so that a new operation can start every cycle; throughput rises and the clock gets faster, at the cost of latency and registers. Hazards are cases where the next instruction cannot proceed: structural (resource conflicts), data (dependencies on results not ready yet, fixed by forwarding and stalls) and control (branches, fixed by prediction and flushing). Balancing stage delays and handling hazards are the main design tasks.

questions.q: Explain pipelining.
questions.st: NVIDIA ASIC Design Engineer interview, Hillsboro
questions.a: Pipelining breaks a task into stages and overlaps them, like an assembly line: while one item is in stage 3, the next is in stage 2 and the one after in stage 1. Each stage has its own register, so after the pipeline fills one result comes out every clock. It increases throughput and allows a higher clock frequency; latency per item increases slightly, and dependencies between items cause hazards.

questions.q: How does pipelining increase a design's clock frequency?
questions.st: NVIDIA Hardware Engineer Internship Santa Clara Ca interview
questions.a: The clock period must cover the longest combinational path between registers. Inserting pipeline registers cuts a long path into shorter ones, so the worst stage delay, and therefore the minimum period, gets smaller: ideally a path of delay T split into k balanced stages allows a period of about T/k plus register overhead (clock-to-Q, setup and skew). The overhead limits the gain from very deep pipelines.

questions.q: What are the stages of a 5-stage pipelined processor?
questions.st: NVIDIA Hardware Intern Santa Clara California interview
questions.a: Instruction Fetch (read the instruction at PC from instruction memory and compute PC + 4), Instruction Decode (decode, read the register file, sign-extend immediates, detect hazards), Execute (ALU operation, address calculation, branch comparison), Memory access (load or store data memory), and Write Back (write the result to the register file).

questions.q: A 100 um wire has 100 us of delay. Buffers with 30 us delay are inserted at 20 um and 50 um. What is the new total delay?
questions.st: NVIDIA Asic Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: Wire delay grows with the square of length (distributed RC), so the 100 um wire's 100 us scales as L^2. Segments of 20, 30 and 50 um give 100 x (0.2^2 + 0.3^2 + 0.5^2) = 100 x 0.38 = 38 us of wire delay, plus 2 buffers x 30 us = 60 us, so about 98 us in total: slightly better than 100 us. (Equal segments would do better; with a linear wire model the buffers would only add delay.)

questions.q: Explain packed versus unpacked arrays in depth.
questions.st: NVIDIA Asic Engineer Santa Clara California interview
questions.a: Packed dimensions are declared before the name (bit [7:0][3:0] p) and are stored contiguously as one vector, so the whole array can be used as a number, sliced, and assigned with arithmetic; only bit-level types can be packed. Unpacked dimensions come after the name (int u [4][8]) and are separate elements, which can be of any type, are accessed element by element, and are how memories are modelled. You can mix them: logic [7:0] mem [0:255] is 256 unpacked bytes.

questions.q: Explain the main ATPG concepts.
questions.st: NVIDIA Dft Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: ATPG automatically generates test patterns for a fault model, usually stuck-at and transition faults on a scan design. For each fault it activates the fault (sets the faulty node to the opposite value), propagates the effect to a scan flop or output, and justifies the required values back to controllable inputs (D-algorithm, PODEM, FAN). Fault simulation then drops all other faults the pattern detects, and pattern compaction merges patterns. Results are reported as fault coverage and test coverage; untestable and redundant faults are classified separately.

questions.q: Find patterns that detect given faults.
questions.st: NVIDIA Dft Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: For each fault, first activate it: set the faulty line to the opposite of its stuck value. Then sensitise a path to an output: set every side input of gates along the path to its non-controlling value (1 for AND and NAND, 0 for OR and NOR). Finally justify all those values back to the primary inputs. Write the resulting input vector and verify that the good and faulty circuits give different outputs; one vector often detects several faults.

questions.q: Find the error in a MUX-based programmable delay circuit.
questions.st: NVIDIA Asic Engineer Santa Clara California interview
questions.a: A programmable delay line built from a chain of delay cells with multiplexers that select a tap. Typical errors: glitches when the select changes while the signal is high (change the select only when the input is stable, or resynchronise it), unequal mux delays making the steps non-monotonic, an inverted or reversed select ordering, missing buffering between taps, and not accounting for PVT variation of the delay cells. Check monotonicity and glitch-free switching.

questions.q: Given a pulse-detector circuit, identify the cases where it fails.
questions.st: NVIDIA Asic Clocks Engineer San Jose California interview
questions.a: A pulse detector usually samples a signal with flops and compares current and delayed values. It fails when the pulse is shorter than a clock period (it can fall between two edges and be missed), when the input is asynchronous and not synchronised (metastability), when two pulses come closer than the detector's recovery time, at reset or power-up when the delayed copy is X, and when glitches create false detections. The fix is to synchronise, stretch short pulses or use a toggle-based crossing.

questions.q: How does a given RC network behave at different frequencies?
questions.st: NVIDIA System Validation Engineer United States interview
questions.a: Treat capacitors as open at low frequency and as short at high frequency (inductors the reverse), then see which path dominates. For an RC network that means finding whether the output is taken across C (low-pass: passes DC, rolls off above 1/(2 pi R C)) or across R (high-pass: blocks DC, passes high frequencies). Around the corner frequency the gain is -3 dB and the phase 45 degrees; beyond it, the gain falls at 20 dB per decade per pole.

questions.q: What is the difference between reg and wire?
questions.st: NVIDIA Asic Engineer Santa Clara California interview
questions.a: A wire is a net: it has no storage and must be continuously driven, by an assign statement or a module output. A reg is a variable that holds the last value assigned to it in an always or initial block. Despite its name, a reg does not have to be a register: in always @(*) it becomes combinational logic. SystemVerilog replaces both in most code with logic, which can be driven either way (by a single driver).

questions.q: Why are fuses important in an SoC?
questions.st: NVIDIA ASIC Design Engineer New Grad interview
questions.a: Fuses (eFuses or anti-fuses) are one-time-programmable bits blown at test time or in the field. They store chip-specific data that must survive power-off: memory repair information (which redundant rows or columns replace failing ones), trimming values for analog blocks and PLLs, unique IDs and calibration, secure boot keys and security settings, and feature or SKU configuration. questions.q: Explain the main features of the APB and AHB protocols.
questions.st: NVIDIA Asic Verification Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: APB is the simple, low-power peripheral bus: no pipelining, a two-phase transfer (setup with PSEL, then access with PENABLE), an optional PREADY for wait states and PSLVERR for errors, used for register access. AHB is a higher-performance bus: pipelined address and data phases, bursts (incrementing and wrapping), wider data, a single master per transfer with arbitration in multi-master systems, HREADY for wait states and HRESP for errors. AXI goes further with separate channels and outstanding transactions.

questions.q: Find the maximum element in a rotated (shifted) sorted array.
questions.st: NVIDIA ASIC Verification Engineer interview, India
questions.a: Use a modified binary search for the rotation point: compare a[mid] with a[hi]; if a[mid] > a[hi], the drop (and the maximum just before it) is in the right half, otherwise in the left. The maximum is the element just before the minimum (or the last element if the array is not rotated). This is O(log n); with duplicates it can degrade to O(n).

questions.q: For a given circuit, calculate the maximum clock frequency.

Also check hold separately (Tclk-to-Q + Tcomb,min >= Thold + skew), because hold does not depend on frequency.

questions.q: How do you write RTL that is efficient in power, performance or area?
questions.st: NVIDIA Asic Engineer interview
questions.a: Performance: pipeline long paths, balance stages, avoid deep priority logic, use one-hot FSMs, and register outputs. Power: gate clocks with enables, avoid unnecessary toggling (operand isolation, hold data when not valid), and reduce memory accesses. Area: share resources such as adders and multipliers across cycles, avoid redundant logic and over-wide signals, prefer RAMs over flop arrays, and keep reset only where needed. Every choice trades one against another.

questions.q: Draw the Bode plot of an op-amp's gain versus frequency.
questions.st: NXP Hardware Intern India interview
questions.a: An internally compensated op-amp has a very high DC gain (100 dB or more) that stays flat up to a low dominant pole (often a few Hz to tens of Hz), then falls at -20 dB per decade, crossing 0 dB at the unity-gain bandwidth (the gain-bandwidth product, for example 1 MHz). The phase drops to -90 degrees after the dominant pole; a second pole near or beyond unity gain sets the phase margin. Closed-loop gain G gives a bandwidth of about GBW / G.

questions.q: Explain how a CMOS inverter works.
questions.st: NXP Hardware Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: A PMOS connects the output to VDD and an NMOS connects it to ground, with both gates on the input. Input low: the PMOS is on and the NMOS off, so the output is pulled to VDD. Input high: the NMOS is on and the PMOS off, so the output goes to 0. Only during the transition do both conduct briefly. In steady state no current flows, so static power is almost zero and the output swings rail to rail.

questions.q: Explain the operating regions of a CMOS inverter.
questions.st: NXP Dft Intern Engineer India interview
questions.a: As the input rises: (1) NMOS off, PMOS linear, output high; (2) NMOS saturated, PMOS linear, output starts falling; (3) both saturated around the switching threshold, highest gain; (4) NMOS linear, PMOS saturated; (5) PMOS off, NMOS linear, output low. The steep middle region is where the inverter amplifies and where noise margins are defined.

For digital signals, the edges matter more than the clock frequency: use the rise time, BW = 0.35 / t_rise (for example a 350 ps edge needs at least 1 GHz, ideally more). Match the probe bandwidth and loading too.

questions.q: What is a demultiplexer, and what is it used for?
questions.st: NXP Hardware Engineer India interview
questions.a: A demultiplexer routes one input to one of several outputs selected by the select lines: with n select bits it has 2^n outputs, and the unselected outputs are 0. It is a decoder with a data input used as the enable. Uses: distributing data to one of several destinations, address decoding (enabling one memory chip or register), and serial-to-parallel conversion.

questions.q: What is the difference between RAM and ROM?
questions.st: NXP Digital Validation Engineer San Diego California interview
questions.a: RAM (random access memory) can be read and written during normal operation and is usually volatile, losing its contents without power; it holds working data. ROM (read-only memory) holds fixed contents written at manufacture or programming time and is non-volatile; it holds boot code and firmware. Programmable variants (PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, flash) blur the line but are still mainly read.

questions.q: What is the difference between a mutex and a semaphore?
questions.st: NXP Firmware Architect Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: A mutex is a lock with ownership: only the thread that locked it can unlock it, and it protects one critical section. A semaphore is a counter: wait or get decrements it and blocks at zero, signal or put increments it, and any thread can signal; a counting semaphore controls access to N identical resources and can also be used for signalling between threads. A binary semaphore behaves like a mutex without ownership.

questions.q: What is the difference between the Arm WFI and WFE instructions?
questions.st: NXP Firmware Architect Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: Both put an Arm core into a low-power standby state. WFI (wait for interrupt) wakes up on an interrupt or a debug event. WFE (wait for event) wakes up on an event, which can be an interrupt but also an SEV (send event) instruction from another core or the event register already being set; it is typically used in spinlocks, so a core waiting for a lock sleeps until the owner signals the release with SEV.

questions.q: Write a program that swaps two values.
questions.st: NXP Vlsi Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: With a temporary: t = a; a = b; b = t;. Without a temporary, using XOR: a ^= b; b ^= a; a ^= b; (fails if a and b are the same variable or memory location), or with arithmetic: a = a + b; b = a - b; a = a - b; (can overflow). In Verilog, a non-blocking swap works directly: a <= b; b <= a;.

questions.q: Compare SPI and I2C: speed, clock stretching and test cases.
questions.st: NXP Validation Engineer Noida Uttar Pradesh interview
questions.a: SPI uses four wires (SCLK, MOSI, MISO and one chip select per slave), is full duplex, has no addressing or acknowledgement, and runs at tens of MHz. I2C uses two open-drain wires (SCL, SDA) with pull-ups, has 7- or 10-bit addressing, ACK and NACK, multiple masters with arbitration, and slower speeds (100 kHz, 400 kHz, 1 MHz, 3.4 MHz). Clock stretching exists only in I2C: a slave holds SCL low to make the master wait. Test cases: all SPI modes (CPOL and CPHA), chip-select timing, back-to-back transfers; for I2C, address match and mismatch, ACK and NACK, repeated start, clock stretching, arbitration loss, and bus timing at each speed.

questions.q: How are I2C pull-ups configured, and how do you choose their value?
questions.st: NXP Validation Engineer Noida Uttar Pradesh interview
questions.a: Each line (SDA and SCL) has one pull-up resistor to VDD, because devices only drive the lines low. The value is a trade-off: small enough that the RC rise time with the bus capacitance meets the spec (for example 1000 ns at 100 kHz, 300 ns at 400 kHz), so Rmax = t_r / (0.8473 Cbus); large enough that a device sinking 3 mA can pull the line below VOL, so Rmin = (VDD - VOL) / IOL. Typical values are 2.2 k to 10 kohm.

questions.q: Explain the setup time of a flip-flop.
questions.st: NXP Hardware Engineer Noida Uttar Pradesh interview
questions.a: Setup time is the minimum time the D input must be stable before the active clock edge, so the flip-flop can capture it reliably. Internally the master latch needs time for the data to propagate through its input stage before it closes. If data changes inside the setup window, the output may take the wrong value or go metastable. In STA the setup check requires data arrival plus setup time to be no later than the capture clock edge.

Integrate the block scoreboards and add an end-to-end scoreboard for the full data path, use a virtual sequencer to coordinate traffic across interfaces, use the RAL model for register configuration, and focus the tests on interactions between blocks, shared resources, clocks and resets, and system scenarios, with coverage across blocks.

A virtual interface is a handle to a SystemVerilog interface instance, which lets class-based code such as drivers and monitors access the DUT's signals; it is passed in through config_db.

questions.q: Design a MUX in CMOS.
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer India interview
questions.a: A 2:1 MUX in CMOS can be built with two transmission gates: one passes A when S = 0, the other passes B when S = 1, with an inverter generating S-bar (6 transistors, or 8 with an output buffer). A static complementary version implements y = A S' + B S as an AND-OR-invert followed by an inverter, which restores the level and drives loads better.

questions.q: Design a summing circuit with an op-amp. What happens if you swap the inverting and non-inverting inputs?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware interview experience, SoC verification (on-campus)
questions.a: An inverting summing amplifier: each input goes through its own resistor Ri into the inverting input, a feedback resistor Rf goes from the output to the inverting input, and the non-inverting input is grounded. Then Vout = -Rf (V1/R1 + V2/R2 + ...). If you swap the inputs (feedback to the non-inverting input), the feedback becomes positive, so the circuit no longer settles at a linear operating point: the output saturates at a rail and behaves like a comparator or latch.

questions.q: Draw a CMOS NAND gate. Does its logic change if the inputs have different delays?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Coimbatore interview
questions.a: Two PMOS in parallel from VDD to the output and two NMOS in series from the output to ground. The logic function does not change with different input delays: in steady state the output is always NAND of the inputs. But the timing does: the delay depends on which input switches (the NMOS nearer the output is faster because the lower node is precharged) and glitches can occur when the inputs change at different times.

questions.q: Draw a CMOS inverter and explain how it works. What happens if VDD is removed?
questions.st: Interview experience for Qualcomm (hardware)
questions.a: PMOS from VDD to the output, NMOS from the output to ground, gates tied to the input. A low input turns the PMOS on (output high); a high input turns the NMOS on (output low). If VDD is removed (floating or 0), the output can no longer be driven high: for a low input it floats or follows leakage, and for a high input the NMOS still pulls it low. The inverter stops working and its inputs may back-power the supply through ESD diodes.

questions.q: Draw a CMOS inverter and mark all four terminals.
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience (on-campus)
questions.a: Each transistor has four terminals: gate, source, drain and body. For the PMOS (pull-up), the source and body connect to VDD, the gate to the input, and the drain to the output. For the NMOS (pull-down), the source and body connect to ground, the gate to the input, and the drain to the output. Tying the bodies this way keeps the junctions reverse biased.

questions.q: Draw a NAND gate in CMOS and explain how it works.
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience (on-campus)
questions.a: PMOS A and PMOS B in parallel between VDD and the output; NMOS A and NMOS B in series between the output and ground. When both inputs are 1, both NMOS conduct and both PMOS are off, so the output is 0. If either input is 0, its PMOS pulls the output to 1 and the series NMOS path is open. The pull-down and pull-up networks are duals, so there is never a static path from VDD to ground.

questions.q: Draw an AND gate using transistors.
questions.st: Qualcomm Design Verification Engineer interview, United States
questions.a: A CMOS AND gate is a NAND gate followed by an inverter: two parallel PMOS and two series NMOS make the NAND, then a PMOS and NMOS pair inverts it, 6 transistors in total. There is no single-stage non-inverting CMOS AND gate, because static CMOS stages are naturally inverting.

questions.q: Draw logic gates at transistor level.
questions.st: Qualcomm Asic Engineer interview
questions.a: Inverter: one PMOS to VDD and one NMOS to ground. NAND: parallel PMOS, series NMOS. NOR: series PMOS, parallel NMOS. AND and OR: a NAND or NOR followed by an inverter. XOR: a complementary implementation with 12 transistors, or transmission-gate versions with 6 to 8. General rule: series NMOS for AND, parallel for OR, and the PMOS network is the dual.

questions.q: Draw the cross-section of a CMOS gate.
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Hyderabad interview
questions.a: On a p-type substrate, the NMOS sits directly in the substrate with n+ source and drain diffusions and a p+ body tap to ground; the PMOS sits in an n-well with p+ source and drain diffusions and an n+ well tap to VDD. Both have a thin gate oxide under a polysilicon or metal gate, separated by shallow trench isolation, with contacts up to the metal layers. The well and substrate taps prevent latch-up.

questions.q: Draw the physical cross-section of an NMOS transistor.
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience (on-campus)
questions.a: A p-type substrate (body) with two heavily doped n+ regions (source and drain), a thin gate oxide over the channel region between them, and a polysilicon or metal gate on top, with spacers on the sides. A p+ body contact ties the substrate to ground, and shallow trench isolation separates it from neighbouring devices. When the gate voltage exceeds Vt, an inversion layer of electrons forms the channel between source and drain.

questions.q: Draw the transfer characteristic of an inverter.
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience (on-campus)
questions.a: Plot Vout against Vin: Vout stays at VDD for low inputs, drops steeply around the switching threshold VM (about VDD/2 for a balanced inverter), and settles at 0 for high inputs. Mark VIL and VIH where the slope is -1, VOH and VOL at the rails, and the noise margins NMH = VOH - VIH and NML = VIL - VOL. A steep transition means high gain and good noise immunity.

questions.q: Explain negative feedback in an op-amp.
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware interview experience, SoC verification (on-campus)
questions.a: Part of the output is fed back to the inverting input, so the op-amp drives its output in the direction that reduces the difference between its inputs. With very high open-loop gain, the inputs stay at almost the same voltage (the virtual short), and the closed-loop gain is set by the feedback network, for example -Rf/Rin, independent of the op-amp's gain. Negative feedback stabilises the gain and extends bandwidth, lowers distortion and output impedance, at the cost of gain.

questions.q: Find the fanout of a gate from its IOH, IOL, IIH and IIL currents.
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience 2020
questions.a: Fan-out is how many inputs one output can drive while staying within logic levels. Compute it for both states: fan-out(low) = IOL / IIL and fan-out(high) = IOH / IIH, and take the smaller of the two. For example IOL = 16 mA, IIL = 1.6 mA gives 10; IOH = 0.4 mA, IIH = 40 uA gives 10, so the fan-out is 10.

questions.q: Find the switching threshold of a CMOS NOR2 gate with Vtn = 2Vtp and Kp = 2Kn.
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience 2020
questions.a: Treat the gate as an equivalent inverter. With both inputs switching together, the two series PMOS act like one with half the strength (Kp/2 = Kn here) and the two parallel NMOS like one with double strength (2 Kn). Setting the currents equal in saturation: 2 Kn (VM - Vtn)^2 = Kn (VDD - VM - |Vtp|)^2, so VM = (VDD - |Vtp| + sqrt(2) Vtn) / (1 + sqrt(2)), and with Vtn = 2 |Vtp| that becomes VM = (VDD + (2 sqrt(2) - 1) |Vtp|) / (1 + sqrt(2)). If only one input switches, the pull-down is a single NMOS and VM shifts higher.

questions.q: What is a ring oscillator?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware interview experience, SoC verification (on-campus)
questions.a: A ring oscillator is an odd number of inverters connected in a loop. There is no stable state, so a transition travels around the ring forever, giving a square wave with period 2 N td (N stages of delay td). It is used to measure gate delay and process speed on test chips, as a VCO (with current-starved stages) in PLLs, and as an on-chip clock or random-number source.

questions.q: What is latch-up in CMOS?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer India interview
questions.a: In bulk CMOS, the parasitic PNP (in the n-well) and NPN (in the substrate) bipolar transistors form a PNPN thyristor between VDD and ground. A current injection (from ESD, overshoot, radiation or a supply glitch) can turn both on, each feeding the other, and they latch into a low-resistance path that draws large current until the power is removed, possibly destroying the chip. Prevention: well and substrate taps close together, guard rings around IO, lower well resistance, spacing between NMOS and PMOS, and SOI processes.

questions.q: What is the switching threshold voltage of an inverter?
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience (on-campus)
questions.a: The switching threshold VM is the input voltage at which Vout = Vin, the middle of the transfer curve where both transistors are in saturation. Equating their currents gives VM = (Vtn + r (VDD - |Vtp|)) / (1 + r), with r = sqrt(kp / kn). With equal strengths (PMOS about 2 to 3 times wider), VM is about VDD/2; a stronger PMOS raises it and a stronger NMOS lowers it.

questions.q: Which is faster, PMOS or NMOS? Why?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Hyderabad interview
questions.a: NMOS is faster: electrons have about 2 to 3 times the mobility of holes, so an NMOS of the same size conducts more current and switches a load faster. That is why PMOS transistors are made wider to match, why NAND gates (series NMOS) are preferred over NOR gates (series PMOS), and why pull-down paths are the fast ones.

questions.q: A 1 uF DRAM capacitor holds 10 uC and is refreshed every 12.5 ms. What are its discharge current and voltage?
questions.st: Qualcomm online test questions 2021 (with ARM post)
questions.a: The stored voltage is V = Q / C = 10 uC / 1 uF = 10 V. If the cell must not lose more than its whole charge before the refresh after 12.5 ms, the maximum allowed leakage (discharge) current is I = Q / t = 10 uC / 12.5 ms = 0.8 mA; in practice you allow only a fraction of the charge to leak (for example 10% gives 80 uA), so that the sense amplifier still reads the right value.

questions.q: Differences between SRAM and DRAM. Why is SRAM used for cache?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware interview experience, SoC verification (on-campus)
questions.a: SRAM uses a 6-transistor latch per bit: fast (around 1 ns access), no refresh, made in the standard logic process, but about 4 to 6 times larger per bit. DRAM uses a capacitor and one transistor: dense and cheap, but slower, with destructive reads, refresh, and a special process. Caches need low latency and must sit on the same die as the core, so SRAM is used; DRAM is used for main memory where capacity matters more.

questions.q: Explain C memory layout, and the size of each type in memory (including bool).
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Validation Engineer Cork County Cork interview
questions.a: A C program's memory has text (code), read-only data (constants and string literals), initialised data (.data), zero-initialised globals and statics (.bss), the heap (malloc, growing up) and the stack (locals and return addresses, growing down), plus memory-mapped IO in embedded systems. Sizes are platform dependent: char 1 byte, short 2, int usually 4, long 4 or 8, long long 8, float 4, double 8, pointers 4 or 8, and bool (C99 _Bool) usually 1 byte, not 1 bit. Structs add padding for alignment.

questions.q: Explain a complete pipeline, stage by stage, with an example.
questions.st: Qualcomm Cpu Verification Engineer Austin Tx interview
questions.a: Take lw x5, 8(x6) followed by add x7, x5, x8. Fetch: the lw is read from instruction memory at PC. Decode: registers are read (x6) and the immediate 8 is extended; the add follows one cycle behind. Execute: the ALU computes x6 + 8. Memory: the data cache is read at that address. Write-back: the value goes into x5. The add needs x5 in its execute stage, one cycle too early, so the hazard unit inserts one bubble and forwarding passes the loaded value from MEM/WB to the ALU.

questions.q: Explain cache coherence with its state diagram.
questions.st: Qualcomm Asic Verification Engineer Santa Clara California interview

questions.q: Explain how a 5-stage pipeline works.
questions.st: Qualcomm Design Verification Engineer interview, Raleigh
questions.a: Five instructions are in flight at once, each in a different stage: fetch from instruction memory, decode and register read, execute in the ALU, memory access, and write-back to the register file. Pipeline registers between stages hold each instruction's data and control signals. After the pipeline fills, one instruction completes every cycle. Hazards are handled with forwarding paths, a load-use stall, and branch prediction or flushing.

questions.q: Explain pipelining, the pipelining paradox, and CPU throughput and speedup.
questions.st: Interview experience for Qualcomm (hardware)
questions.a: Pipelining overlaps instruction execution in stages, raising throughput. Ideal speedup over a non-pipelined design is the number of stages k: n instructions take (k + n - 1) cycles instead of n k. The paradox is that pipelining makes each instruction slower (extra register delay per stage), yet the program runs faster, because more instructions finish per unit time. Real speedup is limited by unbalanced stages, register overhead and hazard stalls: throughput = 1 / (cycle time x CPI).

questions.q: Explain the structure of an SoC and a microprocessor chip.
questions.st: Qualcomm Pre Silicon Verification Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: A microprocessor chip is mainly the CPU cores with caches, an interconnect, a memory controller and IO links. An SoC integrates a whole system: CPU clusters, GPU, DSPs and accelerators, memory controllers, on-chip SRAM, a DMA engine, peripherals (UART, SPI, I2C, USB, PCIe), security and boot blocks, clocks, reset and power management, all connected by an on-chip bus or network (AMBA AXI, AHB, APB or a NoC).

questions.q: How does a GPU pipeline work, including the command streamer?
questions.st: Qualcomm Senior Graphics Hardware Design Verification Engineer Cork interview
questions.a: The driver writes command buffers into memory; the command streamer (front end) fetches and parses them, sets state and dispatches work. In a graphics pipeline, vertices are fetched and processed by vertex shaders, assembled into primitives, clipped and rasterised into fragments, the fragments are shaded by pixel shaders and textured, then depth and stencil tests and blending write the result to the framebuffer. Compute work is dispatched as thread groups across the shader cores (SIMT warps), with caches and memory controllers feeding them.

questions.q: How many 8 KB chips do you need for a 256 KB memory?
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience 2020
questions.a: 256 KB / 8 KB = 32 chips. Each 8 KB chip needs 13 address lines (2^13 = 8192), and the full 256 KB needs 18 address lines; the top 5 lines go to a 5-to-32 decoder that selects one chip.

questions.q: Is SRAM volatile or non-volatile, and why?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware interview experience, SoC verification (on-campus)
questions.a: SRAM is volatile: each bit is held by the feedback of two cross-coupled inverters, which needs power to keep running. When power is removed, the latch loses its state, and at power-up it settles to a random value. Unlike DRAM it needs no refresh while powered.

questions.q: What are cache lines, dirty lines and the dirty bit?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware interview experience, SoC verification (on-campus)

questions.q: What are the performance trade-offs between cache architectures?
questions.st: Qualcomm Design Verification Engineer Intern Santa Clara Ca interview
questions.a: Larger caches lower the miss rate but raise hit latency, area and power. Higher associativity reduces conflict misses but costs hit time and energy. Larger lines exploit spatial locality but waste bandwidth and raise miss penalty. Write-back saves bandwidth versus write-through but adds complexity. Inclusive hierarchies simplify coherence but waste capacity; exclusive ones maximise capacity. Multi-level hierarchies balance fast small L1s with large L2s and L3s.

questions.q: What is a watchdog timer?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware interview experience, SoC verification (on-campus)
questions.a: A watchdog timer is a hardware counter that resets or interrupts the system if software fails to refresh (kick) it within a timeout. Normal software periodically restarts the timer; if the code hangs, crashes or loops, the timer expires and the watchdog resets the chip, recovering from faults without human intervention. Windowed watchdogs also flag refreshes that come too early.

questions.q: Write pipelined code for the fetch and decode stages of a MIPS processor.
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Hyderabad interview
questions.a: Fetch: on each clock, PC <= next_pc; the instruction memory output and PC + 4 go into the IF/ID register (flushed on a taken branch, held on a stall). Decode: split the instruction into opcode, rs, rt, rd and immediate fields, read the register file, sign-extend the immediate, generate the control signals, and write them all into the ID/EX register. The hazard unit compares ID's source registers with a load in EX and stalls (holding PC and IF/ID and zeroing the ID/EX control) when needed.

questions.q: How is the scan DEF generated?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: After scan insertion, the DFT tool writes a scan DEF file that describes the scan chains: each chain's start and stop points, the ordered list of scan flops, and which segments may be reordered (floating or ordered sections, partitions). The place-and-route tool reads it to reorder the chains based on placement, shortening scan wires, and then writes an updated chain order that ATPG must use.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a lockup latch in a scan chain?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: A lockup latch is inserted between scan flops in different clock domains (or with skewed clocks, or opposite edges) on a scan chain. It holds the data for half a cycle, so a late-clocked receiving flop does not capture the new value already shifted out of the earlier flop, avoiding hold violations during shift. It is a level-sensitive latch transparent on the opposite phase of the launching clock.

questions.q: A 20 W and a 60 W bulb are in series across 120 V. Which glows brighter?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Applications Engineer San Diego Ca interview
questions.a: The 20 W bulb. Rated at 120 V, R = V^2 / P gives 720 ohm for the 20 W bulb and 240 ohm for the 60 W bulb. In series they carry the same current, I = 120 / 960 = 0.125 A, so the power is I^2 R: 11.25 W in the 20 W bulb and 3.75 W in the 60 W bulb. The higher-resistance bulb gets more power and glows brighter.

questions.q: Add two numbers without using the + operator.
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer India interview
questions.a: Use XOR for the sum without carries and AND for the carries: while (b != 0) { c = (a & b) << 1; a = a ^ b; b = c; } return a;. Other options: a - (-b), or incrementing in a loop, but the bitwise version is what interviewers expect because it mirrors a hardware adder.

questions.q: Explain short-circuit current.
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Short-circuit (crowbar) current flows while a CMOS gate switches: during the input transition, when the input is between Vtn and VDD - |Vtp|, both the PMOS and the NMOS are on, giving a direct path from VDD to ground. It is larger with slow input slews and with fast outputs, and adds about 10 to 20% to dynamic power. Keeping input transitions sharp and balancing input and output slews reduces it.

questions.q: Explain the MOSFET regions of operation and current equations.
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Coimbatore interview
questions.a: Cut-off (VGS < Vt): ID is about 0 (only subthreshold leakage, exponential in VGS). Linear or triode (VDS < VGS - Vt): ID = k [(VGS - Vt) VDS - VDS^2 / 2], a voltage-controlled resistor for small VDS. Saturation (VDS >= VGS - Vt): ID = (k/2)(VGS - Vt)^2 (1 + lambda VDS). Here k = mu Cox W/L. Short-channel devices show velocity saturation, making ID closer to linear in VGS.

questions.q: Explain your current role and responsibilities in design verification.
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience, Design Verification Engineer (Engineer III)
questions.a: Describe your scope in one breath: the blocks or subsystems you verify, the methodology (UVM, formal, emulation), and your ownership (test plan, testbench architecture, VIP, coverage closure, regressions, sign-off). Then give one concrete example: the hardest bug you found, how you found it and its impact, plus numbers (coverage, bugs, tape-outs). Mention how you work with designers and architects.

questions.q: For a 1000 um net, how do you compute its RC values?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Get the per-unit-length resistance and capacitance for the layer from the technology file or the extraction tables: R per um = sheet resistance / width (plus via resistance), C per um = area, fringe and coupling capacitance for that layer, width and spacing. Multiply by 1000 um: for example 0.1 ohm/um gives 100 ohm and 0.2 fF/um gives 200 fF. Model the wire as a distributed RC (several pi segments) and its Elmore delay is about 0.5 R C plus the driver resistance times the total capacitance.

questions.q: How do you analyze clock tree reports?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Check the summary first: the number of sinks, maximum insertion delay (latency), global and local skew against targets, transition and capacitance violations, and the number and type of clock buffers. Then look at the worst skew pairs and the longest and shortest paths, clock gating cells, crossings between clock domains that need balancing, and the clock tree's power. Compare pre- and post-route numbers and make sure timing uses the propagated clock.

questions.q: How do you connect components when several transaction types flow between them?
questions.st: Qualcomm Asic Intern West Lafayette In interview
questions.a: Use one analysis imp per transaction type, declared with `uvm_analysis_imp_decl(_a) and `uvm_analysis_imp_decl(_b), so the receiver has separate write_a() and write_b() methods. Alternatively use one analysis FIFO per stream and get from each in its own thread, or a common base transaction class with $cast to the specific type in a single write().

questions.q: How do you detect endianness?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: Store a multi-byte value and inspect its first byte: uint32_t x = 1; little_endian = (*(uint8_t *)&x == 1);. A union of an integer and a byte array works the same way. Most compilers also provide macros (such as __BYTE_ORDER__), and many CPUs have a status bit showing the configured endianness.

questions.q: How do you reduce standby (leakage) power?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Power-gate idle blocks (header or footer switches, with isolation and retention for state), use high-Vt cells on non-critical paths, lower the supply in standby (retention voltage for SRAMs), use reverse body bias, stop clocks and put memories into sleep modes, and choose longer channel lengths where speed is not needed. At system level, shut down whole domains in deep sleep.

Inputs and outputs: set_input_delay and set_output_delay relative to the clock, set_driving_cell (or set_drive) on inputs and set_load on outputs. questions.q: Reduce (P + Y)(P' + Y).
questions.st: Qualcomm online test questions 2021 (with ARM post)
questions.a: (P + Y)(P' + Y) = P P' + P Y + P' Y + Y Y = 0 + Y (P + P') + Y = Y. By the distributive law it is directly Y + P P' = Y.

questions.q: What are the high and low noise margins, and what do they signify?
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience (on-campus)
questions.a: Noise margins measure how much noise a logic level can tolerate. NMH = VOH(min) - VIH(min): how far a high output can drop and still be read as high. NML = VIL(max) - VOL(max): how far a low output can rise and still be read as low. VIL and VIH are where the transfer curve's slope is -1. Larger margins mean better immunity to supply noise, crosstalk and ground bounce.

questions.q: What are the pros and cons of low-Vt and high-Vt cells?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Low-Vt cells switch faster (more drive current) but leak much more, exponentially more as Vt drops. High-Vt cells leak far less but are slower. Designs use multi-Vt optimisation: high-Vt (or standard-Vt) cells everywhere by default to save leakage, and low-Vt only on critical paths that need the speed, swapping cells after timing analysis.

questions.q: What checks are done at each stage of the ASIC flow?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer India interview
questions.a: RTL: lint, CDC and RDC, functional verification and coverage. Synthesis: timing, area and power reports, design rule violations, equivalence (RTL versus netlist), and DFT DRC. Floorplan and placement: congestion, utilisation, timing and power grid. CTS: skew, latency and transitions. Routing: DRC, opens and shorts, timing, signal integrity. Sign-off: STA in all corners and modes, IR drop and EM, DRC, LVS, antenna, density, equivalence on the final netlist, and gate-level simulation.

questions.q: What do noise reports and glitch reports represent?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Noise (signal integrity) reports show crosstalk effects: delta delay (aggressors switching in the same or opposite direction speed up or slow down the victim, affecting setup and hold) and functional noise. Glitch reports show bumps induced on a quiet victim net by coupling from switching aggressors: the glitch height and width compared with the receiving cell's noise immunity, because a large enough glitch can flip a latch or flop. Fixes: spacing, shielding, upsizing victims and downsizing aggressors.

questions.q: What does the volatile keyword do?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: volatile tells the compiler that a variable may change outside the normal program flow (a hardware register, an ISR or another thread), so every read and write in the code must really access memory: the compiler cannot cache it in a register, remove repeated reads, or reorder those accesses. It does not make accesses atomic or add memory barriers.

questions.q: What happens if the body is not tied to the source, or is at a higher voltage than the source?
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience (on-campus)
questions.a: If the source rises above the body (for an NMOS, VSB > 0), the body effect increases the threshold voltage, making the transistor weaker and slower, as in stacked transistors. If the body is at a higher voltage than the source (forward body bias for NMOS), the threshold drops, making it faster but leakier; if it exceeds about 0.6 V, the source-body junction becomes forward biased and conducts, which can trigger latch-up. That is why bodies are normally tied to ground (NMOS) and VDD (PMOS).

questions.q: What is a linker script?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: A linker script tells the linker how to place the program in the target's memory: it defines the memory regions (flash, RAM with their addresses and sizes), maps the output sections (.text, .rodata, .data, .bss, stack and heap, interrupt vectors) to those regions, sets the entry point, and defines symbols (such as the start and end of .bss) that the startup code uses to copy and clear data. It is essential for embedded and bare-metal code.

questions.q: What is a multicycle path?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer India interview
questions.a: A multicycle path is a path that is allowed more than one clock cycle to propagate, because the design only samples its result every N cycles (for example data that is enabled every other cycle). You tell STA with set_multicycle_path N -setup, and usually set_multicycle_path N-1 -hold so the hold check moves back accordingly. The design must guarantee the multicycle behaviour, which should be verified.

questions.q: What is one-hot encoding?
questions.st: Qualcomm Design Verification United States interview
questions.a: One-hot encoding uses one flip-flop per state, with exactly one bit high at a time. Next-state and output logic become simple (often one gate per bit), decoding is fast, and it suits FPGAs with plenty of flops. It uses more flip-flops than binary encoding (N versus log2 N), and needs care to recover from illegal states.

questions.q: What is the SNR of a 16-bit ADC?
questions.st: Qualcomm online test questions 2021 (with ARM post)
questions.a: For an ideal N-bit ADC with a full-scale sine input, SNR = 6.02 N + 1.76 dB. For 16 bits that is 6.02 x 16 + 1.76 = about 98.1 dB. Real converters are lower because of noise and distortion, which the effective number of bits (ENOB) captures.

questions.q: What is the difference between RISC and CISC?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: RISC uses a small set of simple, fixed-length instructions that each take about one cycle, a load-store architecture, many registers and a hardwired control unit, which makes pipelining easy. CISC uses many complex, variable-length instructions with memory operands and multi-cycle execution, often microcoded, for denser code. Modern CISC chips translate instructions into RISC-like micro-ops, so the practical difference is mainly in decode complexity.

questions.q: What is the difference between a structure and a union?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: In a struct each member has its own storage, so the size is at least the sum of its members (plus padding for alignment), and all members are valid at once. In a union all members share the same storage, so the size is that of the largest member and only one member is meaningful at a time. Unions are used to save memory or to view the same bits as different types, such as for endianness checks.

questions.q: What is the difference between modeling and characterization?
questions.st: Qualcomm Soc Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: Modelling builds a description that predicts behaviour, such as a SPICE model of a transistor, a timing model of a cell, or an architecture model of a CPU. Characterisation measures or simulates a real circuit across conditions to extract the numbers that go into a model, for example running SPICE on each standard cell across PVT corners, loads and slews to fill the Liberty timing and power tables. Characterisation feeds the models.

questions.q: What is the difference between sequential and combinational circuits?
questions.st: Qualcomm Dft Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: A combinational circuit's outputs depend only on its present inputs; it has no memory or clock (gates, multiplexers, adders, decoders). A sequential circuit's outputs depend on the present inputs and the stored state, kept in latches or flip-flops, usually updated by a clock (registers, counters, FSMs). Sequential circuits are combinational logic plus memory and feedback.

questions.q: What is the difference in instruction execution between RISC and CISC CPUs?
questions.st: Interview experience for Qualcomm (hardware)
questions.a: A RISC CPU fetches fixed-length instructions that are simple to decode, does arithmetic only on registers, and moves data with separate load and store instructions, so each instruction flows through a simple pipeline in about one cycle. A CISC CPU decodes variable-length instructions that may read memory, compute and write memory in one instruction, traditionally taking many cycles through microcode; modern CISC cores split them into micro-ops that execute like RISC instructions.

questions.q: What is the trade-off between dynamic power and leakage power?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Dynamic power falls with lower voltage and fewer transitions, but lower voltage makes transistors slower, which tempts designers to lower the threshold voltage, and leakage rises exponentially as Vt drops. So reducing dynamic power through voltage scaling increases leakage, and fast low-Vt cells increase leakage too. The balance is set per design with multi-Vt cells, DVFS and power gating: low Vt on critical paths, high Vt elsewhere, and gating to remove leakage when idle.

questions.q: What power-reduction techniques do you know?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Clock gating, multi-Vt cell assignment, power gating with isolation and retention cells, multiple voltage domains, dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, operand isolation, low-power memory modes and memory banking, reducing switching activity through encoding and glitch reduction, and architectural choices such as parallelism at lower voltage. Implementation is driven by UPF power intent and verified with power-aware simulation.

questions.q: Where and when do you use decoupling capacitor (DCAP) cells?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Decap cells are on-chip capacitors between VDD and VSS placed in the standard cell rows. They supply local charge during sudden current demands, reducing dynamic IR drop and supply noise. Place them near high-activity logic (clock buffers, wide buses, register banks), near power-hungry macros and in empty space after placement. They cost area and add some leakage, so use them where dynamic IR analysis shows hotspots.

questions.q: Which addressing mode does MOV AX, [CX] use?
questions.st: Qualcomm online test questions 2021 (with ARM post)
questions.a: It is register indirect addressing: the operand's memory address is held in a register, and AX is loaded from the memory location that the register points to. Note that on the real 8086, only BX, BP, SI and DI can be used as address registers, so MOV AX, [CX] is not a valid 8086 instruction; MOV AX, [BX] is the valid form.

questions.q: Write a sequence item for the input interface of a given scenario.

Register it with the factory and field macros or do_copy and do_compare, and add a convert2string for debug. Keep timing out of the item: the driver handles the handshake.

questions.q: Explain the top-level pin placement flow. What decides it?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Top-level pin placement assigns each IO or block pin to a location on the die or block edge. It is decided by the package and board (bump and ball map, signal grouping), the location of the blocks that connect to each pin (to shorten routes and meet timing), signal type (high-speed pairs and clocks need special placement and shielding), power and ESD needs, and routing congestion. The flow: get the pin list and constraints, place the pins (often guided by a first trial placement), check timing and congestion, then iterate with block owners.

questions.q: Given block netlists, timing constraints, libraries and macro LEFs, how do you start floorplanning?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Read the netlists, libraries (.lib), LEFs and constraints, and check them (missing cells, constraint sanity). Set the die and core size from area and target utilisation, define rows and the IO or pin placement, then place the macros: near their related logic and IO, along edges, oriented to keep pins facing the core, with halos and channels for routing. Build the power grid (rings, straps, macro connections), add blockages and endcap and tap cells, then run a quick placement and timing and congestion checks to refine it.

questions.q: Write binary search in pseudocode and give its time complexity.
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware interview experience, SoC verification (on-campus)
questions.a: lo = 0, hi = n - 1; while lo <= hi: mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if a[mid] == key return mid; else if a[mid] < key then lo = mid + 1 else hi = mid - 1; return not found. The array must be sorted. Time complexity is O(log n) because the range halves each step; space is O(1) for the iterative version.

questions.q: Write merge sort in C and give its time complexity.
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware interview experience, SoC verification (on-campus)
questions.a: void merge_sort(int *a, int *tmp, int lo, int hi) { if (hi - lo < 1) return; int mid = (lo + hi) / 2; merge_sort(a, tmp, lo, mid); merge_sort(a, tmp, mid + 1, hi); int i = lo, j = mid + 1, k = lo; while (i <= mid && j <= hi) tmp[k++] = (a[i] <= a[j]) ? a[i++] : a[j++]; while (i <= mid) tmp[k++] = a[i++]; while (j <= hi) tmp[k++] = a[j++]; for (k = lo; k <= hi; k++) a[k] = tmp[k]; }. Time O(n log n) in every case; space O(n) for the temporary array; it is stable.

questions.q: Explain the AHB protocol.
questions.st: Qualcomm Soc Verification Engineer interview
questions.a: AHB (AMBA High-performance Bus) is a pipelined bus: each transfer has an address phase and a data phase, and the address of the next transfer overlaps with the data of the current one. Key signals: HADDR, HTRANS (IDLE, BUSY, NONSEQ, SEQ), HWRITE, HSIZE, HBURST (single, incrementing and wrapping bursts of 4, 8 and 16), HWDATA and HRDATA, HREADY for wait states and HRESP for errors. A decoder selects the slave, and in multi-master systems an arbiter grants the bus. AHB-Lite is the single-master version.

questions.q: What is the difference between AXI and AHB, in terms of the AXI channels?
questions.st: Qualcomm Design Verification Engineer interview, Bangalore
questions.a: AXI has five independent channels: write address (AW), write data (W), write response (B), read address (AR) and read data (R), each with its own valid and ready handshake. This allows reads and writes at the same time, multiple outstanding transactions, out-of-order completion using IDs, and burst transfers described only by the start address and length. AHB has one shared address and data pipeline, one outstanding transfer per master, in-order responses and separate arbitration, so AXI gives much higher throughput and better latency hiding.

questions.q: Explain UVM callbacks, mailboxes and semaphores.
questions.st: Qualcomm Senior Graphics Hardware Design Verification Engineer Cork interview
questions.a: UVM callbacks let users add behaviour to a component without modifying it: the component calls `uvm_do_callbacks at hook points, and a test registers a callback object (for example to inject errors in a driver). A mailbox is a FIFO for passing objects between threads, with put and get (blocking), try_put and try_get, and an optional size bound. A semaphore controls access to a shared resource with get(n) and put(n) of keys, so only one thread (or n) uses it at a time.

questions.q: Explain the SystemVerilog testbench: interface, clocking block, program block and virtual interface.
questions.st: Qualcomm Design Verification Engineer interview, Bangalore
questions.a: An interface bundles related signals (and can contain tasks, assertions and modports) so the DUT and testbench connect through one port. A clocking block inside it defines when signals are sampled and driven relative to a clock (with input and output skews), which avoids races between testbench and design. A program block runs testbench code in the reactive region, also to avoid races (less used with UVM). A virtual interface is a handle to an interface instance that class-based code (drivers, monitors) uses to reach the signals.

questions.st: Qualcomm Design Verification Engineer Cork interview
questions.a: Concurrent SVA assertions are best placed in the interface (or a checker module bound to the DUT with bind), not in UVM classes, because classes cannot contain concurrent assertions. Write a property on the interface clock with disable iff (reset), assert it with a label and an else $error or `uvm_error message, and add cover properties. Immediate assertions can be used inside classes (for example in the scoreboard or on randomize()). Control them from the test with $assertoff and $asserton or a config knob.

questions.q: How does a uvm_test start?
questions.st: Qualcomm Asic Intern West Lafayette In interview
questions.a: The top module calls run_test(), either with a test name or with +UVM_TESTNAME on the command line. The UVM root uses the factory to create the test as uvm_test_top, then runs the phases on the whole hierarchy: build (the test builds the environment), connect, end_of_elaboration, start_of_simulation, then run_phase where the test raises an objection, starts its sequences and drops the objection; when all objections are dropped, the extract, check, report and final phases run and the simulation ends.

questions.q: How would you formally verify a cache?
questions.st: Qualcomm Formal Verification Engineer San Diego Ca interview
questions.a: Write properties for the cache's correctness and let the tool prove them for all input sequences: data integrity (a read returns the value of the last write to that address), using a symbolic or chosen address and data with a small reference model to keep the state space small; tag and valid consistency; no two ways holding the same tag; correct dirty-bit and write-back behaviour; coherence-protocol invariants (only one Modified copy) and deadlock or liveness properties for the controller. Use abstractions such as reduced sets, ways and data width, and assumptions on the bus protocol.

questions.q: What are the UVM phases and why do we use them?
questions.st: Qualcomm Design Verification Engineer interview, Bangalore
questions.a: UVM phases are the ordered steps every component goes through: build (create sub-components top-down), connect (connect TLM ports), end_of_elaboration and start_of_simulation (final checks and printing), run (the time-consuming test, optionally split into reset, configure, main and shutdown), then extract, check, report and final. They are used so that all components are created before they are connected and connected before they run, without any manual synchronisation, and so that results are collected consistently at the end.

questions.q: What is a deep copy versus a shallow copy in SystemVerilog?
questions.st: Qualcomm Senior Verification Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: A shallow copy (b = new a;) creates a new object and copies a's properties, but any handles inside it are copied as handles, so both objects point to the same sub-objects; changing a nested object through one copy affects the other. A deep copy also creates new copies of every nested object, so the two are fully independent. SystemVerilog only provides the shallow copy built in; a deep copy needs a custom copy() method (in UVM, do_copy) that calls copy on each nested object.

questions.q: What is a virtual interface and why is it used?
questions.st: Qualcomm Senior Verification Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: A virtual interface is a variable that holds a handle to an interface instance. Classes cannot contain interfaces or ports directly because they are dynamic objects, so drivers and monitors use a virtual interface to access the DUT's signals. The top module instantiates the interface and passes it down (in UVM through uvm_config_db), which keeps the class code reusable with any instance of that interface.

questions.q: What is the UVM sequencer used for?
questions.st: Qualcomm Senior Verification Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: The sequencer is the arbiter between sequences and the driver. Sequences generate items and send them to the sequencer with start_item and finish_item; the sequencer arbitrates when several sequences run at once (FIFO, priority, random or user-defined), hands items to the driver through get_next_item, and routes responses back to the right sequence. It also supports locking and grabbing for exclusive access and virtual sequencers for coordination.

questions.q: What is the difference between simulation, emulation and formal verification?
questions.st: Qualcomm interview experience, Design Verification Engineer (Engineer III)
questions.a: Simulation runs the RTL in software with full visibility, easy debugging and 4-state values, but it is slow (around 10 to 1000 Hz for a large SoC). Emulation maps the design onto special hardware (Palladium, ZeBu, Veloce) and runs at around 1 MHz, fast enough to boot an OS and run software, with less but still good visibility. Formal verification does not run cycles at all: it mathematically proves properties for all possible inputs, exhaustive but limited to smaller blocks.

questions.q: What is the difference between tasks and functions in UVM?
questions.st: Qualcomm Asic Intern West Lafayette In interview
questions.a: In UVM, as in SystemVerilog, functions execute in zero simulation time and cannot block, so the build, connect, extract, check and report phases are functions (build_phase, connect_phase); tasks can consume time, so run_phase and the run-time sub-phases (reset_phase, main_phase), sequence body() and driver code are tasks. You cannot call a task from a function, so time-consuming work must stay in task phases.

questions.q: What is the difference between virtual methods and virtual classes in SystemVerilog?
questions.st: Qualcomm Senior Graphics Hardware Design Verification Engineer Cork interview
questions.a: A virtual method can be overridden by a derived class, and calls through a base handle run the derived version at run time (polymorphism). A virtual class is an abstract class: it cannot be instantiated with new, only extended, and it can declare pure virtual methods that every concrete derived class must implement. A virtual class can contain both regular and virtual methods.

questions.q: When building timing constraints, do you need to constrain all I/O ports?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Qualcomm)
questions.a: Yes, in practice every input and output should be constrained relative to a clock with set_input_delay and set_output_delay (plus drive and load), otherwise those paths are unconstrained and never checked. Exceptions: asynchronous inputs such as an asynchronous reset or signals crossing from other domains, which are synchronised and can be false paths or set_max_delay; static configuration pins (case analysis or false path); and analog or test-only ports. Tools report unconstrained ports, which should be reviewed.

questions.q: How do Verilog case statements synthesize?
questions.st: Qualcomm Hardware Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: A case statement in combinational logic becomes a multiplexer selected by the case expression, or a decoder driving the outputs. If the items are mutually exclusive (a full, parallel case), it maps to a parallel mux; overlapping items or casez wildcards give priority logic like an if-else chain. Missing items without a default in combinational logic create latches. In a clocked block, the case logic feeds the flip-flops' D inputs.

questions.q: What are multicycle paths and false paths, and how do you handle them?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hynix)
questions.a: A false path is a path that can never propagate in a real operation (asynchronous crossings with synchronisers, mutually exclusive mux paths, test-only logic): STA should ignore it with set_false_path. A multicycle path is a valid path that is only required to settle in N cycles because the design samples it every N cycles: set_multicycle_path N -setup and N-1 -hold. Both must be justified by the design (and verified, for example with CDC or formal checks), because wrong exceptions hide real violations.

questions.q: What timing-optimization strategies do you use pre-layout and post-layout?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hynix)
questions.a: Pre-layout (synthesis): correct and realistic constraints, logic restructuring, retiming and pipelining, resizing and Vt selection, buffering high-fan-out nets, path groups and physical-aware synthesis. Post-layout: placement optimisation (moving and clustering critical cells), gate sizing and Vt swaps, buffer insertion and removal, useful skew in CTS, layer promotion and non-default rules for critical nets, fixing crosstalk with spacing and shielding, and ECOs, while fixing hold with delay cells after setup is met.

questions.q: How do you optimize power at each stage of the physical design flow?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hynix)
questions.a: Synthesis: clock gating, multi-Vt selection, operand isolation and power-aware mapping. Floorplan: power domains, power switches, macro placement to shorten high-activity wires. Placement: cluster high-activity cells, reduce wire capacitance, use high-Vt cells on non-critical paths. CTS: fewer, well-sized clock buffers and gating close to sinks, since the clock is a large share of dynamic power. Routing and sign-off: reduce wire capacitance, swap leakage-heavy cells to high Vt with timing slack, and verify IR drop and power with real activity.

questions.q: What process-technology challenges affect physical design?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hynix)
questions.a: Advanced nodes bring tighter design rules and multi-patterning constraints (coloring, cut rules), higher wire and via resistance making routing and IR drop harder, more variation (OCV, local variation, aging, self-heating), FinFET discrete widths, stronger crosstalk, EM limits, more corners and modes to close, density and DFM rules, and pin-access problems in dense standard cells. All of these increase runtime and need more margin.
