questions.q: Design asynchronous and synchronous FIFOs at the circuit level.
questions.st: SK Hynix Senior Asic Design Engineer San Jose California interview
questions.a: Synchronous FIFO: a dual-port RAM (or register array), read and write pointers on one clock, and a count or an extra pointer bit to generate full and empty. Asynchronous FIFO: the RAM is written in the write clock domain and read in the read domain; each side keeps binary pointers with one extra bit, converts them to Gray code, and synchronises the Gray pointer into the other domain through two flops. Full is computed on the write side (Gray write pointer equals the synchronised read pointer with the top two bits inverted), empty on the read side (pointers equal); flags are pessimistic but safe.

questions.q: Which RTL coding styles give the best back-end results?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (Hynix)
questions.a: Fully synchronous design with one clock edge, registered outputs and inputs at block boundaries, no latches unless intended, no combinational loops, one clock and reset strategy (synchronous de-assertion), clock gating only through library ICG cells, limited logic depth between registers, avoiding very wide muxes and long priority chains, resource sharing where timing allows, parameterised and readable code, and clean CDC boundaries. These make synthesis, timing closure and DFT smoother.

questions.q: Explain pin-density and cell-density issues, and hotspots.
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (STMicroelectronics)
questions.a: Pin density is the number of cell pins per area; when too many pins sit in a small region, the router cannot reach them all, causing congestion, detours, DRC violations and timing degradation. Cell density (utilisation) that is too high in an area leaves no room for buffering and routing. Hotspots are these local congestion or high-density regions, often near macros or around highly connected logic. Fixes include cell padding, placement density limits, partial blockages, spreading logic, and using cells with better pin access.

questions.q: Explain the ECO methodology.
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (STMicroelectronics)
questions.a: An ECO (engineering change order) applies a small change to a design late in the flow without redoing everything. Functional ECO: the RTL is fixed, then a tool or engineer derives the minimal netlist change (adding, removing or reconnecting a few gates), which is implemented in the placed and routed database using spare cells or new cells, and verified with equivalence checking. Timing ECOs resize cells and insert buffers. After tape-out, metal-only ECOs use pre-placed spare cells so only metal masks change.

questions.q: How do you set variables in Tcl?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (STMicroelectronics)
questions.a: With set: set name value (for example set period 2.5). Read it with $name; set x [expr {$a + 1}] evaluates an expression; lists with set l {a b c} or [list ...]; arrays with set arr(key) value; global variables with global inside procs. Use unset to delete a variable and info exists to test for one.

questions.q: How is IR drop analysis done, and what statistics do the reports give?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (STMicroelectronics)
questions.a: Static IR analysis uses average power per instance (from switching activity) and computes the voltage drop across the power grid resistance; dynamic IR analysis uses time-based current waveforms (vectorless or from simulation activity) to find peak drops when many cells switch together. Reports give the worst drop per net (VDD and VSS), drop maps showing hotspots, per-instance effective voltage, resistance per path, and electromigration current density violations. Fixes include more straps, vias and decaps, and spreading high-activity cells.

questions.q: If too many logic-cell pins sit in one place in the core, what issues arise and how do you resolve them?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (STMicroelectronics)
questions.a: Pin congestion: too many pins to connect in a small area, so the router cannot access them all, causing detours, shorts and opens, DRC violations, longer wires with worse timing and crosstalk. Fix it with cell padding or spreading (placement density screens, partial blockages), using cells with better pin access, avoiding very high-fan-in cells clustered together, reshaping or relocating the logic, and adjusting the floorplan (macro placement, channels).

questions.q: What is the command for setting a multicycle path?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (STMicroelectronics)
questions.a: set_multicycle_path N -setup -from <start> -to <end>, usually with set_multicycle_path N-1 -hold for the same paths so the hold check moves back to the original edge. Use -start or -end to choose which clock's cycles are counted when the launch and capture clocks differ.

questions.q: How do you relate the routing grid to the manufacturing grid, and check the routing grid is set correctly?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (STMicroelectronics)
questions.a: The manufacturing grid is the minimum resolution of all layout coordinates (for example 0.005 um); every shape, pin and track must sit on it. The routing grid (tracks) is defined per layer by a pitch and an offset in the technology LEF; the pitch must be a multiple of the manufacturing grid and should match the cells' pin positions so pins are on or reachable from tracks. Check it by comparing the LEF pitches and offsets with the cell rows and pin locations, running a track and pin-access check, and making sure routed wires produce no off-grid DRC errors.

questions.q: What kinds of routing issues have you faced?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (STMicroelectronics)
questions.a: Typical ones: congestion around macros and in dense logic, pin-access problems in high-density cells, shorts and opens left after detail routing, DRC violations (spacing, minimum area, via enclosure, end-of-line rules), antenna violations on long nets, crosstalk on long parallel nets, timing degradation from detours, and clock nets needing non-default rules and shielding. Describe one you fixed, for example adding channels or blockages, cell padding, or layer assignment.

questions.q: Define a hash and an array in Perl.
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (STMicroelectronics)
questions.a: In Perl, an array is an ordered list indexed by integers, declared with @ (my @arr = (1, 2, 3); $arr[0]). A hash is an unordered set of key-value pairs indexed by strings, declared with % (my %h = (clk => 100, rst => 0); $h{clk}). Arrays keep order and are accessed by position; hashes give fast lookup by name.

questions.q: What is the intrinsic gain of a common-source stage with and without degeneration, and of a simple differential amplifier? How does it change with frequency?
questions.st: SambaNova Hardware Engineer Palo Alto California interview
questions.a: A common-source stage with a current-source load has intrinsic gain gm ro (the maximum, typically 10 to 50 in modern nodes). With source degeneration Rs, the effective transconductance becomes gm / (1 + gm Rs), so the gain falls (about Rd / Rs for large gm Rs) but becomes more linear and predictable. A simple differential pair with a current-mirror load has a differential gain of gm (ro2 || ro4), about half the intrinsic gain. All of them roll off with frequency because of the output pole 1/(Rout CL), and the Miller effect at the input reduces bandwidth further.

questions.q: Draw a CMOS inverter and explain everything you can about it.
questions.st: Samsung Semiconductor Hardware New Delhi interview
questions.a: Cover structure (PMOS pull-up, NMOS pull-down, gates tied), operation (one transistor on at a time), the transfer curve and its five regions, the switching threshold and how sizing sets it, noise margins, delay (charging the load capacitance, rise and fall times, effect of sizing and load), power (dynamic C V^2 f, short-circuit during transitions, leakage), and layout (n-well, contacts, the stick diagram). Mention why it is the reference cell for characterising a technology.

questions.q: What happens if you swap the PMOS and NMOS in a CMOS circuit?
questions.st: Samsung Semiconductor Hardware Engineer Bengaluru interview
questions.a: With the NMOS in the pull-up and the PMOS in the pull-down, each transistor passes the logic level it is bad at: the NMOS can only pull the output up to VDD - Vtn, and the PMOS can only pull it down to |Vtp|. The circuit no longer inverts (it behaves as a degraded buffer through source followers), output levels and noise margins degrade, and the next stages may draw static current.

questions.q: What is punch-through in CMOS?
questions.st: Samsung Design Verification Engineer interview, Bengaluru
questions.a: Punch-through happens in short-channel MOSFETs when the drain depletion region extends far enough to merge with the source depletion region. The gate then loses control of the channel, and a large current flows from drain to source even with the transistor off, similar to breakdown. It is prevented with halo or pocket implants, higher channel doping and shallow junctions, and limits how short the channel can be for a given voltage.

questions.q: Which part of a hardware design holds bit information, and where is it stored?
questions.st: Samsung Semiconductor Senior Hardware Engineer Hwaseong interview

Inside a flip-flop or SRAM cell, the bit is kept by cross-coupled inverters (feedback); in DRAM it is the charge on a capacitor. Combinational logic holds no information: it only computes from the stored bits and the inputs.

questions.q: Explain the CMOS inverter and its characteristics.
questions.st: Synopsys interview experience for intern
questions.a: The CMOS inverter is a PMOS pull-up and an NMOS pull-down with their gates joined. Characteristics: rail-to-rail output, almost no static power, a sharp voltage transfer curve with a switching threshold set by the PMOS-to-NMOS ratio, good noise margins, propagation delay proportional to the load capacitance and inversely to drive current, dynamic power C V^2 f plus short-circuit and leakage power, and very high input impedance (capacitive load).

questions.q: What does a DMA controller do?
questions.st: Synopsys VLSI interview questions 2020
questions.a: A DMA (direct memory access) controller moves data between memory and peripherals, or between memory regions, without the CPU copying every word. The CPU programs source and destination addresses, length and mode (and descriptor chains for scatter-gather), starts the transfer and is free for other work; the DMA performs bus transactions and raises an interrupt when done. It saves CPU time and power and gives higher throughput for bulk transfers.

questions.q: Explain RC integrator and differentiator circuits.
questions.st: Synopsys Analog And Digital Verification Engineer India interview
questions.a: An RC integrator is a series resistor with the output taken across a capacitor to ground: when the time constant RC is much longer than the input's period, the output approximates the integral of the input (a square wave becomes a triangle); it is also a low-pass filter. An RC differentiator has the capacitor in series and the output across the resistor: when RC is much shorter than the period, the output approximates the derivative (a square wave becomes spikes at each edge); it is also a high-pass filter. Op-amp versions give precise integration and differentiation.

questions.q: Explain the SerDes architecture.
questions.st: Synopsys Senior System Architect Mississauga Ontario interview
questions.a: A SerDes converts parallel data to a high-speed serial stream and back. Transmit: encoding (8b/10b, 64b/66b or 128b/130b) and scrambling, a serializer clocked by a high-speed PLL, pre-emphasis or FFE equalisation, and a current-mode or voltage-mode driver. Receive: termination, CTLE and DFE equalisation to undo channel loss, clock and data recovery (CDR) to extract the clock from the data, a deserializer, alignment and decoding. Modern links use PAM4 and ADC-based receivers with DSP.

questions.q: What are LUTs in an FPGA?
questions.st: Synopsys Fpga Prototyping Engineer India interview
questions.a: A LUT (look-up table) is the basic logic element of an FPGA: a small memory with k inputs (typically 4 to 6) that stores the 2^k output bits of a truth table, so it can implement any k-input Boolean function; the inputs act as the address. LUTs are configured by the bitstream and are combined with flip-flops, carry chains and multiplexers in logic blocks. Some LUTs can also be used as small RAMs or shift registers.

questions.q: What are start and stop bits?
questions.st: Synopsys Design Verification Intern Hyderabad Telangana interview
questions.a: In asynchronous serial (UART), the line idles high. A start bit (a 0) marks the beginning of a frame, so the receiver can synchronise its sampling to the falling edge, then the data bits follow (usually LSB first, 5 to 9 bits) with an optional parity bit, and one or two stop bits (1) return the line to idle and give time before the next frame. They let the receiver frame each character without a shared clock.

questions.q: What are the design guidelines for a high-speed board?
questions.st: Synopsys Hardware Engineer Sunnyvale California interview
questions.a: Control impedance (50 ohm single-ended, 100 ohm differential) with a proper stackup and continuous reference planes under every high-speed trace; keep differential pairs tightly coupled and length matched; minimise vias and stubs (back-drill), and avoid crossing plane splits; keep traces short and spaced to reduce crosstalk; terminate correctly; give good power integrity with low-inductance decoupling close to pins and plane capacitance; and simulate signal and power integrity before fabrication.

questions.q: What is a PLL?
questions.st: Synopsys Fpga Prototyping Engineer India interview
questions.a: A phase-locked loop generates a stable, high-frequency clock locked to a reference. A phase-frequency detector compares the reference with the divided output, a charge pump and loop filter turn the error into a control voltage, and a voltage-controlled oscillator produces the output; a divider by N in the feedback makes fout = N x fref. PLLs are used for clock multiplication, de-skewing, frequency synthesis and clock recovery.

questions.q: Why is isolation needed in a UPF power intent? How do you handle isolation and retention across multiple power domains?
questions.st: Synopsys Senior Applications Engineer Portland Oregon interview
questions.a: When a power domain is switched off, its outputs float or go to unknown values, which can cause wrong logic and crowbar current in the always-on domains that receive them. Isolation cells clamp those signals to a known value (0, 1 or the last value) while the domain is off, enabled by an isolation signal from the power controller. Retention keeps register state during shutdown using retention flops with a separate always-on supply and save and restore signals. In UPF: set_isolation with -clamp_value, -isolation_signal and location; set_retention with save and restore signals; and a power controller sequence (isolate, save, power off; power on, restore, release isolation).

questions.a: A combinational loop is logic that feeds back to itself without a register. In RTL it usually comes from a signal assigned in terms of itself in an always @(*) block, or from two blocks feeding each other; lint and synthesis tools report them.

questions.q: How does an always block run if it has no sensitivity list?
questions.st: Synopsys interview questions based on synthesis and simulation
questions.a: An always block with no sensitivity list and no timing control (always begin a = b; end) runs forever in zero time: it loops again immediately, so simulation time never advances and the simulator hangs. Every always block needs a sensitivity list (@(...)) or a delay or event control inside, for example always #5 clk = ~clk; for a clock generator.

Latches, combinational loops and incomplete sensitivity lists usually give warnings rather than errors.

questions.q: What happens to an oscillating circuit in RTL synthesis and in simulation?
questions.st: Synopsys interview questions based on synthesis and simulation
questions.a: A combinational loop with an odd number of inversions (like a ring oscillator in RTL) has no stable state. In simulation it oscillates in zero time or with the given delays: with zero delays the simulator iterates forever in one time step and hangs or hits an iteration limit. Synthesis does not model oscillation; it warns about a combinational loop and builds the gates anyway, and static timing breaks the loop arbitrarily. Real oscillators should be designed as custom or library cells.

questions.q: What is casex used for in Verilog?

It is used for priority decoding. Its risk is that X values from uninitialised signals also match, hiding bugs in simulation; casez (only Z and ? are wildcards) or SystemVerilog case inside are safer.

questions.q: What is the difference between true and false data dependencies?
questions.st: Tenstorrent Design Verification Engineer Los Angeles California interview
questions.a: A true dependency (RAW, read after write) is real data flow: an instruction needs the value produced by an earlier one, so it must wait or be forwarded. False dependencies come from reusing register names, not from data flow: WAR (write after read, an anti-dependency) and WAW (write after write, an output dependency). Register renaming removes false dependencies by giving each write a new physical register.

questions.q: Draw a CMOS inverter and explain how it works.
questions.st: Texas Instruments interview experience, Digital Design Engineer 2023
questions.a: A PMOS from VDD to the output and an NMOS from the output to ground, with both gates on the input. A low input turns the PMOS on and the NMOS off, pulling the output up to VDD; a high input turns the NMOS on and the PMOS off, pulling it to ground. Only one network conducts in steady state, so no static current flows, and the output swings fully between the rails.

questions.q: Draw a non-inverting op-amp and write its gain.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Validation Engineer Austin Texas interview
questions.a: Input to the non-inverting (+) terminal, a feedback resistor Rf from the output to the inverting (-) terminal, and Rg from the inverting terminal to ground. Gain = Vout / Vin = 1 + Rf / Rg. It is always at least 1, the input impedance is very high, and Rf = 0 (with Rg open) gives a unity-gain buffer (voltage follower).

questions.q: Draw an inverter's voltage transfer curve and explain each region.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Design Verification Engineer Dallas Texas interview
questions.a: Plot Vout against Vin from 0 to VDD. Region 1: NMOS off, PMOS linear, Vout = VDD. Region 2: NMOS in saturation, PMOS linear, Vout starts to drop. Region 3: both in saturation at the switching threshold VM, the steepest part with high gain. Region 4: NMOS linear, PMOS saturated. Region 5: PMOS off, NMOS linear, Vout = 0. Mark VIL and VIH where the slope is -1 to define the noise margins.

questions.q: Draw an inverting op-amp amplifier and derive its gain.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Validation Test Engineer United States interview
questions.a: Input through Rin to the inverting (-) terminal, Rf from the output to the inverting terminal, and the non-inverting terminal grounded. The inverting input is a virtual ground, so the current through Rin, Vin / Rin, all flows through Rf (the op-amp input draws no current): Vin / Rin = -Vout / Rf, so the gain is Vout / Vin = -Rf / Rin.

questions.q: Draw an inverting op-amp and derive its output.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Product Test And Validation Richardson Texas interview
questions.a: With the non-inverting input grounded, negative feedback holds the inverting input at virtual ground. The current Vin / Rin flows through Rf, so Vout = -(Rf / Rin) Vin. The output is inverted and scaled by the resistor ratio, and the input impedance is Rin.

questions.q: Draw the CMOS circuits of NAND and NOR gates.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Verification Engineer Dallas Texas interview

questions.q: Draw the PMOS and NMOS transistors separately and mark their terminals.
questions.st: Texas Instruments interview experience, Digital Design Engineer 2023
questions.a: Each MOSFET has four terminals: gate, source, drain and body. The NMOS symbol has the arrow on the source or body pointing inward (or out from the channel on the source), the PMOS has the arrow pointing outward and often a bubble on the gate. In circuits, the NMOS source and body usually go to ground and the PMOS source and body to VDD; current flows from drain to source in an NMOS and from source to drain in a PMOS.

questions.q: Draw the cross-section of a transistor and explain the body effect.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Design Verification Engineer Dallas Texas interview
questions.a: NMOS cross-section: p-type substrate, n+ source and drain, thin gate oxide and a gate above the channel, with a p+ body contact. The body effect: when the source is at a higher potential than the body (VSB > 0), the depletion region under the gate widens, more charge is needed to invert the channel, and the threshold voltage rises: Vt = Vt0 + gamma (sqrt(2 phiF + VSB) - sqrt(2 phiF)). It weakens stacked transistors and source followers.

questions.q: Explain CMOS technology and its advantages over other technologies.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Hardware Intern Israel interview
questions.a: CMOS uses complementary NMOS and PMOS networks, so in steady state there is no path from supply to ground: static power is almost zero. Compared with bipolar, NMOS-only or TTL logic, CMOS gives much lower power, full rail-to-rail swing and high noise margins, very high input impedance and fan-out, high density, and it scales well with process shrinks, which is why almost all digital ICs use it. Its costs are speed per gate versus bipolar (historically), leakage in advanced nodes and latch-up.

questions.q: Explain a CMOS concept you know, for example the CMOS inverter and its gate capacitance.
questions.st: Texas Instruments interview experience for internships (on-campus)
questions.a: Pick one and explain it fully. For example the CMOS inverter: structure, the transfer curve, the switching threshold set by sizing, noise margins, and delay. Its gate capacitance is the input load seen by the driving gate: roughly Cox W L plus overlap capacitances for both transistors, varying with the operating region; the Miller effect makes the gate-drain capacitance appear larger during switching. This capacitance sets the delay of the previous stage and the dynamic power C V^2 f.

questions.q: How does an inverter's delay change when its load capacitance changes?
questions.st: Texas Instruments digital interview questions 2021
questions.a: The delay grows roughly linearly with load capacitance: t_d is about 0.69 Reff (Cload + Cpar), where Reff is the equivalent resistance of the driving transistor and Cpar its own drain capacitance. Doubling the load roughly doubles the load-dependent part of the delay and slows the output slew, which slows the next stage too. Upsizing the inverter lowers Reff but increases its input capacitance.

questions.q: What is breakdown voltage? Draw the V-I curve of a diode in forward and reverse bias.
questions.st: Texas Instruments interview experience, Digital Design Engineer 2023
questions.a: The breakdown voltage is the reverse voltage at which a diode suddenly conducts large current, through avalanche multiplication or Zener tunnelling. The V-I curve: in forward bias, almost no current until about 0.6 to 0.7 V for silicon, then the current rises exponentially; in reverse bias only a tiny leakage current flows until the breakdown voltage, where the current rises sharply at a nearly constant voltage (which Zener diodes use for regulation).

questions.q: What is the output voltage of an inverting op-amp?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Design Verification Engineer Dallas Texas interview
questions.a: For an ideal inverting amplifier, Vout = -(Rf / Rin) Vin. For several inputs in a summing configuration, Vout = -Rf (V1/R1 + V2/R2 + ...). The output is limited by the supply rails, so it saturates if the ideal result exceeds them.

questions.q: What limits an op-amp's bandwidth?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Verification Engineer Dallas Texas interview
questions.a: The gain-bandwidth product, set by the dominant-pole compensation that keeps it stable, which makes the gain fall at -20 dB per decade, so closed-loop bandwidth is about GBW divided by the closed-loop gain. For large signals the slew rate also limits the bandwidth (full-power bandwidth = SR / (2 pi Vpeak)). Load capacitance and the second pole reduce phase margin, which in practice limits usable bandwidth too.

questions.q: Why does a virtual short appear between op-amp inputs?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Analog Applications Engineer India interview
questions.a: With negative feedback and a very large open-loop gain A, the output Vout = A (V+ - V-) stays finite, so the input difference must be tiny (Vout / A, microvolts). The inputs therefore sit at almost the same voltage, which is the virtual short, while no current flows into them because of the high input impedance. If the non-inverting input is grounded, the inverting input is a virtual ground.

questions.q: How do SRAM reads and writes behave when the pass-gate resistance is large?
questions.st: Texas Instruments digital interview questions 2021
questions.a: Larger pass-gate (access transistor) resistance makes reads more stable but slower: the cell discharges the bit line more slowly, so the read takes longer, but the storage node is disturbed less (a better read static noise margin). Writes become harder: the bit-line driver has to overpower the cell's pull-up through a weaker path, so writes slow down and can fail at low voltage. SRAM sizing balances the pull-down, pass-gate and pull-up ratios for both.

questions.q: How would you verify the interface between a memory and a CPU?

Test single and burst reads and writes, byte enables and alignment, back-to-back and outstanding transactions, address boundaries, wait states and back-pressure, error responses for invalid addresses, reset during transfers, and ordering rules. Add protocol assertions on the interface and coverage on transaction types, sizes and addresses.

questions.q: What is the voltage after charge sharing among stacked capacitors?
questions.st: Texas Instruments digital interview questions 2021
questions.a: Charge is conserved on the node(s) that are connected when the switch closes. Write the total charge before (sum of C_i V_i for capacitors referenced to the same node), then after connection all connected capacitors share one voltage: V_final = sum(C_i V_i) / sum(C_i). For capacitors stacked in series, the same charge flows through each, so the voltage splits in inverse proportion to capacitance. Energy is lost in the switch resistance.

questions.q: Why does a DMA controller have multiple channels, and how do they operate in parallel?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Validation Engineer Bangalore Rural Karnataka interview
questions.a: Multiple channels let several independent transfers be set up at once (for example audio, UART, SPI and memory copies), each with its own source, destination, length, priority and trigger. They share the bus, so an arbiter interleaves their transfers in time (round-robin or priority) at burst granularity; with multiple bus ports or a crossbar, some can run truly in parallel. Peripheral request lines start the matching channel, and each raises its own interrupt when done.

questions.q: A Zener rated for 10 mA is in series with 1 kOhm across a 10 V source. What current flows in the Zener?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Hardware Intern Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: It depends on the Zener voltage Vz, which the question needs. If Vz is below 10 V, the Zener regulates and the current is I = (10 - Vz) / 1 kohm, for example 4.9 mA for a 5.1 V Zener, well within the 10 mA rating (the maximum, 10 mA, would only happen with Vz = 0). If Vz is above 10 V, the Zener never breaks down and almost no current flows.

questions.q: Compare the power of an AND gate driven by 200 MHz and 400 MHz clocks with tying both inputs to one clock.
questions.st: Texas Instruments digital interview questions 2021
questions.a: Dynamic power is the sum over nodes of alpha C V^2 f. With 400 MHz and 200 MHz clocks on the two inputs (aligned, 50% duty), the inputs toggle at 400 and 200 MHz, and the output is high only when both are high, giving a 200 MHz pulse train with 25% duty, so the output switches at 200 MHz. With both inputs tied to one clock, the output simply follows that clock: at 400 MHz the output switches twice as often (plus both inputs at 400 MHz); at 200 MHz all nodes switch at 200 MHz. Compare by adding the switching rate of each node times its capacitance.

questions.q: Explain SDF back-annotation and the SPEF timing-correlation flow.
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (TI)
questions.a: After place and route, parasitic extraction writes the wire resistances and capacitances to a SPEF file. The STA tool reads the netlist, libraries and SPEF, computes cell and net delays, and checks timing. It can write the computed delays to an SDF file, which gate-level simulation back-annotates onto the netlist to simulate with real delays. Correlation means checking that delays from different tools agree: for example, the place-and-route tool's internal timing against sign-off STA with sign-off extraction, adjusting margins or settings when they differ.

questions.q: Explain an RC low-pass filter.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Analog Mixed Signal Ams Verification Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: A series resistor and a capacitor to ground, with the output across the capacitor. At low frequencies the capacitor's impedance is high, so the output follows the input; at high frequencies the capacitor shorts the output to ground. The cut-off frequency fc = 1/(2 pi R C) is where the output is -3 dB (0.707 of the input) with a -45 degree phase shift; above it the gain falls at 20 dB per decade. In the time domain, a step input gives an exponential rise with time constant RC.

questions.q: Explain how a MOSFET works.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Hardware Engineer Intern Calcutta West Bengal interview
questions.a: A MOSFET has a gate separated from the channel region by a thin oxide. For an NMOS, a gate voltage above the threshold attracts electrons to the surface, forming a conducting channel between the n+ source and drain (inversion). The gate voltage controls the channel's conductivity, so the drain current is controlled by voltage with almost no gate current. With small VDS it acts as a resistor (linear region); with larger VDS the channel pinches off near the drain and the current saturates. A PMOS works the same way with holes and opposite polarities.

questions.q: Explain the timing-closure flow: methodology, issues and fixes.

Close setup first: fix the worst paths by logic restructuring, sizing, Vt swaps, buffering, useful skew and floorplan or placement changes; at the RTL level, pipeline or retime. After CTS, fix hold with delay cells without breaking setup. After routing, handle crosstalk and the extracted parasitics, and analyse all corners and modes with OCV derates. Iterate with ECOs until every path meets timing in sign-off STA. Common issues: bad constraints, congestion detours, long nets, and setup-hold conflicts.

questions.q: Given a digital circuit with a fault, which inputs detect it in one pass?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Validation Engineer Dallas Texas interview
questions.a: Activate the fault and propagate it: set the faulty node to the value opposite its stuck value using the primary inputs, then set the side inputs of every gate on a path from that node to an output to their non-controlling values (1 for AND and NAND, 0 for OR and NOR) so the difference reaches the output. Justify all of these values back to the inputs; the resulting input vector detects the fault in a single pass, since the good and faulty circuits produce different outputs.

questions.q: Given a post-route database and functional fixes, how do you implement an ECO, and what physical and functional checks do you run?

Implement them in the routed database: use spare cells for metal-only changes or place new cells near the affected logic, then route the changed nets incrementally. Checks: logical equivalence between the new RTL and the ECO netlist, STA for setup, hold and transitions across corners, DRC, LVS and antenna, IR drop if large, and DFT (scan chains still intact).

questions.q: Given one gate's rise time and the load capacitances, find another gate's rise time.
questions.st: Texas Instruments digital interview questions 2021
questions.a: For the same driver, the rise time is proportional to the load capacitance (t is about 2.2 R C for 10% to 90%), so t2 = t1 x C2 / C1. If the drivers differ, scale by their drive strengths too: t2 = t1 x (R2 C2) / (R1 C1). Include each gate's own output (parasitic) capacitance in C if given.

questions.q: How can a half-bridge rectifier give the same result as a full-bridge rectifier?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Analog Applications Engineer Dallas Texas interview
questions.a: A half-wave rectifier passes only one half of the AC cycle, so its output has gaps and more ripple. To get full-wave rectification with only two diodes, use a centre-tapped transformer: each half of the secondary feeds one diode, so both half cycles produce current through the load in the same direction, giving the same output as a full-bridge (but each half of the winding only supplies the peak of its own half, so the transformer needs twice the secondary voltage).

questions.q: How do you measure an unknown resistance with a voltmeter and an ammeter?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Validation Engineer Munich Bavaria interview
questions.a: Put the ammeter in series with the resistor and the voltmeter in parallel across it, apply a known voltage, and compute R = V / I. For a small resistance, connect the voltmeter directly across the resistor (the ammeter outside it), so the ammeter's resistance does not add to the measurement; for a large resistance, put the ammeter right next to the resistor inside the voltmeter's connection, so the voltmeter's current does not add to the measured current.

It is used to look at waveforms, measure amplitude, frequency, rise time, jitter and timing relationships between signals, and to debug glitches and noise.

questions.q: Name five measurable characteristics of a clock signal.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Validation Engineer Dallas Texas interview
questions.a: Frequency (or period), duty cycle, rise and fall times, amplitude and voltage levels (overshoot and undershoot), jitter (period, cycle-to-cycle, phase jitter), phase noise, and skew relative to another clock.

questions.q: Simplify a 5-variable function with a K-map.
questions.st: Texas Instruments digital interview questions 2021
questions.a: Draw two 4-variable K-maps, one for E = 0 and one for E = 1, side by side. Group 1s within each map as usual, and also between the maps: a cell in one map is adjacent to the same cell in the other map. A group that appears in the same position in both maps drops the variable E. Write the minimal sum of products from the largest groups. Quine-McCluskey is the systematic alternative for 5 or more variables.

questions.q: Sketch the output of an RC filter without s-domain analysis.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Asic Engineer Chennai Tamil Nadu interview
questions.a: Think in terms of the capacitor's voltage not changing instantly and the time constant tau = RC. For an RC low-pass with a step input, the output rises exponentially toward the input, reaching 63% after one tau and nearly 100% after 5 tau; a square wave gives rounded edges if the period is long compared with tau and a triangle-like wave if it is short. For an RC high-pass, the output jumps with the input edge, then decays exponentially to 0.

questions.q: What are BJTs and MOSFETs, and how do they differ?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Product Validation Engineer Dallas Texas interview
questions.a: A BJT (bipolar junction transistor) is a current-controlled device with an emitter, base and collector: a small base current controls a larger collector current (Ic = beta Ib), with high transconductance and good matching, but it draws base current. A MOSFET is a voltage-controlled device with a gate, source, drain and body: the gate voltage controls a channel, with essentially no DC gate current and very high input impedance. MOSFETs dominate digital and dense ICs; BJTs remain in analog, RF and power niches.

questions.q: What happens when two capacitors are connected in series?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Hardware Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: Capacitors in series carry the same charge, so the total capacitance is lower than the smallest one: 1/C = 1/C1 + 1/C2 (for two, C = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2)). The applied voltage divides in inverse proportion to capacitance, V1 / V2 = C2 / C1, so the smaller capacitor takes the larger voltage. Series connection is used to raise the voltage rating or to make capacitive dividers.

questions.q: What is the average output voltage of a switched resistor circuit with 40% on-time?
questions.st: Texas Instruments digital interview questions 2021
questions.a: The average equals the duty cycle times the voltage applied when the switch is on: for a source V switched across the resistor 40% of the time and 0 otherwise, the average output is 0.4 V (for example 4 V from 10 V). If an RC filter follows, the output settles to that average with some ripple.

questions.q: What is the difference between combinational and sequential circuits?
questions.st: Texas Instruments interview experience for internships (on-campus)
questions.a: A combinational circuit's output depends only on its current inputs (no memory), like adders and multiplexers. A sequential circuit's output depends on its current inputs and its stored state, held in flip-flops or latches and usually updated by a clock, like counters, registers and state machines.

questions.q: What is the high-frequency content of a PWM signal?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Design Verification Engineer Dallas Texas interview
questions.a: A PWM signal is a square wave at the switching frequency whose average (the low-frequency content) carries the wanted signal. The high-frequency content is the switching frequency and its harmonics (plus sidebands around them from the modulation), which must be filtered out with a low-pass filter (or the load's own inductance) to recover the average. Sharp edges add harmonics far above the switching frequency, which matters for EMI.

questions.q: Why choose a particular feedback resistor value, and what changes if its rating changes?
questions.st: Texas Instruments System Verification Engineer Pune Maharashtra interview
questions.a: In a feedback network the resistor value sets the gain (for example Gain = 1 + Rf/Rg) or the regulator output voltage, and its absolute value trades current consumption (larger values draw less), noise (larger values add more thermal noise and are more sensitive to input bias currents and leakage) and bandwidth (larger values form slower poles with stray capacitance). If the value changes, the gain or output voltage changes with it; tolerance and temperature coefficient matter for accuracy; and the power rating must cover the dissipation.

questions.q: What issues have you faced with clock gates at each stage of the physical design flow?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (TI)
questions.a: At synthesis, the integrated clock gating cells must be inserted correctly and their enable timing checked (clock gating setup and hold). At placement, gating cells must sit near their flops, or the enable path becomes critical. At CTS, gating cells add clock insertion delay and skew, so the tree must balance gated and ungated sinks, and the enable timing changes once the clock is propagated. After routing, crosstalk on enables and clock nets. Typical fixes: cloning gating cells, moving them closer to the sinks, and constraining the enable paths.

questions.q: Write a program that prints 'hattrick' when a string has three consecutive w's.
questions.st: Texas Instruments interview experience, Digital Design Engineer 2023
questions.a: Scan the string with a counter: for each character, if it is 'w' increment the counter, otherwise reset it to 0; when the counter reaches 3, print 'hattrick' (and decide whether overlapping runs count again). In Python: if 'www' in s: print('hattrick'). In hardware it is a small FSM or a 2-bit counter on the serial character stream.

questions.q: Explain UVM testbench components, phases and TLM ports.
questions.st: Texas Instruments Asic Design Verification Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: Components: the test, environment, agents (sequencer, driver, monitor), scoreboard, coverage collectors, and sequences and sequence items, all created through the factory and configured with config_db. Phases order the work: build, connect, end_of_elaboration, start_of_simulation, run (with optional reset, configure, main and shutdown sub-phases), extract, check, report and final. TLM ports connect components: the seq_item port between driver and sequencer, analysis ports for one-to-many broadcast from monitors, and put, get and FIFO ports for point-to-point transfers.

questions.q: How are timing constraints developed?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (TI)
questions.a: Start from the specification: clocks (sources, frequencies, duty cycle, generated clocks), their relationships (synchronous or asynchronous groups), and the IO timing from the interface specs or the budgets of neighbouring blocks (input and output delays, drive and load). Add clock uncertainty for jitter and skew, then exceptions such as false paths, multicycle paths and case analysis for modes, justified by the design. Validate the constraints with checks (unconstrained paths, clock coverage) and refine them as the design matures.

questions.q: What is the difference between SystemVerilog and UVM?
questions.st: Texas Instruments Analog Mixed Signal Ams Verification Engineer Bengaluru Karnataka interview
questions.a: SystemVerilog is a language: a hardware description and verification language that extends Verilog with classes, constraints, coverage, assertions and interfaces. UVM is a methodology and class library written in SystemVerilog: it provides a standard structure (components, phases, factory, config_db, TLM, sequences, reporting) for building reusable testbenches. You need SystemVerilog to use UVM, but you can write testbenches in SystemVerilog without UVM.

questions.q: What synthesis strategies optimize timing?
questions.st: Companywise ASIC/VLSI interview questions (TI)
questions.a: Write tight, correct constraints, then: higher compile effort and incremental optimisation, ungrouping hierarchy so logic can be optimised across boundaries, register retiming, path groups to focus on critical paths, critical-range optimisation, resizing and low-Vt cells on critical paths, buffering and register duplication for high-fan-out nets, and physical-aware (topographical) synthesis for realistic wire delays. At the RTL level, pipeline long paths and restructure deep logic.
